Flujo de Anclas Cinematográficas

Un ancla es la imagen fija que el modelo de video va a heredar. Todo lo crítico se fija en el still antes de animar: identidad, composición, aspect ratio, texto visible y estado del producto. El video amplifica cualquier ambigüedad del still. Este flujo clasifica cada ancla en nueve dimensiones, elige la técnica de producción según el tipo de acción y el número de personas, y la lleva por lints, generación, crítica y canonización hasta el motion brief.

Definición
Qué es un ancla y qué hereda el video de ella
Roles posibles de un ancla
Character ref: maestro de identidad. Front, three-quarter, profile, back para Kling Elements; luz pareja, sin sombras duras que el modelo confunda con rasgos, fondo limpio, 1080p o más, sin texto.
Environment ref: placa de entorno vacía; su texto es series_lock.environment verbatim.
Keyframe FF: primer frame del clip. Fija identidad, layout y texto en imagen; el prompt de video describe solo cómo evoluciona.
Keyframe LF: último frame. Mismo aspect ratio que el FF o el modelo lo estira; se declara por separado del FF en Seedance.
Hero o macro: producto, objeto ancla, inserto de detalle.
Lo que el video hereda y ya no se puede corregir
Aspect ratio: se genera en el ratio destino, nunca se recorta después de animar.
Identidad y vestuario: el video repite el identity block, pero la cara la fija el still.
Dirección de luz: window-left se queda window-left en todos los clips.
Geometría espacial: dónde está el héroe, dónde la amenaza, hacia dónde escapa.
Qué tercio ocupa el cuerpo, punto de vista, dirección de viaje, manos nombradas en contactos.
nano-banana.md · consistency-locks Lock 7 · dramaturgy §8 · forge Rule 6
Lo que un ancla nunca lleva
Texto en pantalla: capa separada, text-overlays.json.
Logos y lettering de marca generados: solo heredados de asset aprobado o compuestos en post.
Movimiento descrito: un still es un instante congelado; el movimiento se prompt como su residuo físico.
Vocabulario prohibido: cinematic, epic, stunning, masterpiece, beautiful lighting, emociones nombradas sin cuerpo.
forge Rule 1 y 6 · SW30 R8 R10 · director §6.1 · animatic-keyframes §4

Se elige por la dinámica de poder del beat, nunca por variedad. D9 por tipo de acción: el ángulo como decisión, no como variedad
| Tipo de acción | Ángulo y altura por defecto | Por qué | Cuándo romperlo | Fuente

| B instante pico | Low o a ras de la superficie, aislando al sujeto contra cielo o agua; nivel del agua para la ruptura | El pico se lee como fuerza; el fondo limpio deja ver la consecuencia física | Top-down para el patrón de la salpicadura o la geometría del impacto | animatic §6 INFERENCIA

| C movimiento continuo | Altura de parachoques o más baja; rig montable; larga focal a nivel de pista para compresión | Cue a del presupuesto de velocidad; el ángulo alto y limpio es el god-angle que mata la velocidad | Un plano alto solo como proof shot lejano de espacio cubierto | race §3 §5 §10

| D fenómeno de luz | Low con horizonte bajo para cielo y evento; silueta de paisaje o figura contra la fuente | La fuente motivada domina si ocupa el frame; la figura a contraluz da escala | High para lluvia sobre un patrón urbano | race §7 contre-jour INFERENCIA

| E interacción | Eye-level y OTS; el que domina más alto o en la puerta; eje de 180 grados respetado entre plano y contraplano | Staging revela la jerarquía antes del diálogo; la altura relativa es señal de poder | Low o high sobre un personaje en el beat de Shift, con rationale de continuidad de luz | dramaturgy §6 · Lock 7 · visual-media regla de 180

| F multitud anónima | High o aérea para escala y patrón; low con la masa como muro para amenaza | El ángulo decide si la multitud es paisaje o presión | Eye-level dentro de la masa solo con héroe canonizado en MG | animatic §6 angle encodes the beat · race §3 crowd at periphery

Doce pasos y cinco gates. La ruta por tipo de acción es la bifurcación que cambia la técnica; el resto del flujo es común. Ninguna ancla se genera sin sus dependencias canonizadas ni sin tarjeta completa.
Paso 3 · dimensión D2
Seis tipos de acción y cómo se congela cada uno

Un still no puede mostrar movimiento ni emoción: prompt el residuo físico que cada uno deja. Los cuatro ejemplos del brief están cubiertos: el auto de carreras es tipo C, la clavadista entrando al agua es tipo B, el rayo es tipo D, las dos personas en el café son tipo E.
| Tipo | Ejemplos | Cue de movimiento congelado | Qué debe estar en el prompt | Qué lo mata | Check del crítico añadido | Fuente

| A pose sostenida | Retrato documental, persona esperando, objeto ancla en reposo cargado, maestro de identidad | Quietud deliberada: cero blur, bordes duros, reloj parado. O vector de postura que solo puede resolverse hacia adelante | Anatomía solo en decisión: nombrar el verbo de la mano. Micro-acción en el cuerpo, una presión ambiental, un motivo. Para maestros: luz pareja, fondo limpio, sin sombras duras | Anatomía en reposo sin verbo, objeto estático sin cambio de estado, "beautiful establishing shot" | Tres detalles presentes; la pose tiene vector o es un maestro de identidad declarado | animatic §4 §5 · dramaturgy §2 §3 · kling §7

| B instante pico | Clavadista entrando al agua, gota, impacto de balón, tirón de tela, fractura de chocolate | Blur parcial congelado: el elemento en movimiento apenas barrido, el ancla nítida. Un diezmilésimo de segundo arrestado | Boardear el estado posterior del umbral: el agua ya abriéndose, la espuma con borde iluminado, gotas como constelación specular con rim en el borde de ataque. Física por consecuencia: qué provocó la acción, no la acción. "frozen mid-" explícito | Pedir "diving" o "splashing" como verbo abstracto; equal blur; describir la acción sin su consecuencia | El estado posterior es visible y físicamente coherente; el blur es diferencial; la anatomía en el pico es correcta al zoom | animatic §4 §5 · U9 consequence prompting · SW30 R8 · race §3 smoke/spray

| C movimiento continuo | Auto de carreras, ciclista, corredor, dron, tren, caballo al galope | Barrido direccional del fondo con héroe nítido; llantas y rayos barridos a disco; referencia de primer plano alargada en varilla de luz | Presupuesto de velocidad: al menos 3 de 5: cámara a la altura del parachoques o más baja, asfalto barriendo el borde inferior, referencia cercana pasando el borde, héroe nítido contra fondo barrido, cue de vibración mecánica. El rig debe poder montarse en el vehículo | Ángulo alto y limpio de belleza, cabina perfectamente estable, rim nítido en auto en movimiento, aire alrededor del auto, un solo cue | Contar los cues: menos de 3 es una foto de auto. Rim barrido. Textura de asfalto visible. Sin panel que solo funcione acelerado | race-and-speed §1 §3 §6 §10 · animatic §4

| D fenómeno de luz o clima | Rayo cortando el cielo, explosión de flash, amanecer sobre el edificio, lluvia sobre una ventana, tormenta de arena INFERENCIA | El evento está completamente formado, no naciendo: el rayo entero, el suelo ya iluminado por él. Quietud del paisaje contra la violencia de la luz | El fenómeno es la fuente de luz motivada: núcleo blanco quemado, halación, el mundo a contraluz o rimado por él, sombras duras que solo esa fuente puede dar. Una presión ambiental, no tres apiladas. Nombrar grano, bloom, negros aplastados | Fenómeno más luz de estudio contradictoria, atmósfera frontal (humo o lluvia frontal es gris muerto), humo + niebla + spray en el mismo still | Una sola fuente domina la escena; las sombras son coherentes con el evento; la atmósfera está a contraluz | dramaturgy §9 Kurosawa · race §7 backlit smoke, specular · U8 no contradictions · animatic §7 anti-sterile

| E interacción o diálogo | Dos personas conversando en un café, entrega de objeto, abrazo, high five, confrontación | Micro-acción del cuerpo en el punto de contacto o de mirada: nudillos, mandíbula, hombro angulado; el gesto que revela el deseo oculto | Staging antes que diálogo: quién domina de pie o sentado, quién en la puerta, quién tras el vidrio, espacio negativo, encuadre apretado. Eyelines nombradas. Manos nombradas en cualquier contacto. Producción en pasos: placa del café → inserto A → inserto B; el contacto lo fija el keyframe aprobado, nunca la asignación de manos por texto | Dos personas en una sola génesis, "left half" como posición, dos manos derechas, cambio de dirección de luz en el contraplano sin rationale | Dinámica de poder legible sin leer el guion; eyelines correctas; contacto anatómico al zoom; luz consistente entre plano y contraplano | dramaturgy §5 §6 · SW30 R1 R2 R4 R7 R9 · forge Rule 6 handedness · Lock 7 · critique Layer 4 eye-line

| F multitud anónima | Estadio, manifestación, gente corriendo por la calle, público de concierto. Un grupo con identidades no es tipo F: ver ensamble en D3 | Profundidad en tres planos: héroes nítidos en MG, multitud como textura en FG y BG, rostros fragmentados, siluetas, espaldas, contraluz | La multitud es entorno, no sujetos: se produce como placa con figuras anónimas y sin rostros legibles, después se insertan los héroes canonizados uno por uno. Máximo 3 héroes con identidad; cada uno con su propia referencia y rol. Forzar diferenciación: ropa, pelo y rasgos distintos, movimientos no sincronizados, "no identical clones in the background". Multitud en movimiento, manifestación o carrera callejera: la multitud se trata como textura barrida con las cues de velocidad del tipo C | Pedir N rostros distintos desde texto, clones del héroe entre los extras, caras que se funden, más de 3 identidades sin referencia individual | Contar rostros legibles: todos los legibles son héroes canonizados; ningún extra clona al héroe; los planos FG/MG/BG tienen trabajos distintos | fixes twins/face-blending · kling §7 3+ characters only with own element · U13 · race §3 crowd at periphery · animatic §6 §7 · nano-banana multi-reference · SW30 R1 R7

Cuatro huecos en las skills instaladas. Los tipos B, D y F, y el grupo ensamble de D3, no tienen sección propia en ninguna fuente. El tipo B se deriva del método de motion-as-still y del consequence prompting; el D de las reglas de atmósfera a contraluz y de fuente motivada; el F de la corrección de gemelos y del límite de personajes de Kling; el ensamble de los límites de referencias por modelo y de la disciplina de roles U13. Las reglas marcadas como inferencia deben canonizarse después de probarse con un caso real, igual que se hizo con el template de rostro.
Paso 3 · dimensiones D2 × D3
Tratamiento de personas: técnica según número de sujetos y tipo de acción

La regla madre es SW30 regla 1: un solo trabajo por generación. Todo lo demás es cómo respetarla cuando la escena pide más de una persona. Hay dos casos que no se parecen: la multitud anónima, donde nadie tiene rostro legible y la masa es entorno, y el grupo ensamble, un quinteto de cuerdas o un grupo de K-pop, donde cada miembro es un héroe con identidad, vestuario e instrumento propios y todos deben reconocerse en el mismo frame.

Cada rostro legible en el frame es una identidad que hay que sostener en todos los clips. Por eso el crítico cuenta rostros: los que no son héroes canonizados se convierten en silueta, espalda o desenfoque, o el ancla no pasa.

| EN.6 | Crítico por miembro: capa Series Lock se corre N veces, cada rostro contra su maestro; manos e instrumentos con lateralidad correcta; ningún rostro sin dueño | critique-rubric Layer 2 y 5 · forge Rule 6 handedness | Un rostro que no corresponde a ningún maestro es REJECT, no REVISE
Paso 4 · dimensiones D4 a D7
Tratamiento artístico: defaults de cámara, luz, paleta y textura

El tratamiento fija los valores por defecto de las otras tres dimensiones y qué está prohibido. Se declara una vez por proyecto y se repite verbatim en cada ancla; cambiarlo a mitad de serie produce el fallo 6 del forge, la serie que "se siente distinta" con todos los locks puestos.
| Tratamiento | Cámara y lente | Luz | Paleta y grade | Textura y stock | Rostros | Prohibido | Fuente

Handoff al video: el motion brief
El ancla aprobada entra al modelo de video con un prompt corto que solo dice cómo evoluciona. Describir lo que ya está en la imagen provoca deriva de identidad.

Consecuencia para la base de reglas: las ocho dimensiones de la tarjeta de ancla son facetas de consulta. Un brief de "clavadista olímpica entrando al agua, documental, un sujeto, keyframe FF para Kling" filtra por D2 = B, D3 = 1, D4 = documental, D1 = FF, D9 = low a ras de agua, D8 según rostro visible, y trae exactamente las reglas de física por consecuencia, blur parcial, luz dura, template de piel si hay rostro, y las de imagen a video de Kling. Sin la tarjeta, la consulta devuelve el catálogo entero.

La tarea más compleja que resuelve el sistema de skills, descompuesta en cinco niveles: el megaflujo, sus ocho etapas, los subprocesos de cada etapa, la taxonomía de activos génesis de la que depende toda la producción visual, y el subflujo atómico que produce uno de esos activos sin ninguna referencia adjunta. Un activo génesis es cualquier sujeto que el pipeline necesita fijar en imagen antes de que exista una referencia de él. Las fuentes distinguen seis clases, y la clase decide modelo, archivo de patrón, bloques del prompt y qué puede heredar de él lo que viene después. Nivel 4

Seis clases de sujeto génesis. La única bifurcación de salida es la marca: un producto con logo o etiqueta real no puede nacer de texto, porque el logo solo puede heredarse de un asset aprobado; se convierte en un flujo con referencia. | Producto | Packaging, comida, bebida, cosmético, device | PR | PROD | GPT Image 2 quality high para etiquetas, materiales y condensación; NBP para distorsión física creíble | No relevante | Logos y lettering solo heredados de asset aprobado (SW30 R10); sin marcas en frame, se componen en post (forge R6). Los cuerpos nunca tapan un logo | Hero shot, inserto macro, producto en manos del sujeto

| Objeto / prop | El objeto ancla, herramienta, vehículo, mobiliario | PR | PROD | Cualquiera; NBP si el objeto tiene física o transparencia | Sí para especies vegetales; no para objetos genéricos | Reaparece en varios shots como motivo (dramaturgy §13), así que se canoniza como una persona. Legible en macro y en plano general | Detalle, macro insert, continuidad del motivo entre clips

Principio de dos pasos. La génesis fija solo la parte del sujeto que lleva la identidad; todo lo que la extiende es un paso posterior con esa génesis adjunta como referencia. En una persona la identidad vive en el rostro, así que el orden es retrato de rostro T1 → cuerpo entero T2 con el rostro como Image 1 → cuadros T3 y T4. En un animal, la cabeza y el pelaje primero, las poses después. En un producto, el hero shot frontal primero, el producto en escena después. Fuentes: SW30 reglas 1, 5 y 11; image/characters.md "Identity Locking"; nano-banana.md, fallos conocidos: los rostros y las manos derivan, y NBP a veces sostiene peor los rostros que NB2.

Hueco detectado en la base de reglas. La taxonomía de casos actual solo tiene T1 y T2 para personas y PROD para todo lo que no es persona. Lugar genérico, edificación o landmark, animal y objeto no tienen código propio, y las reglas de grounding, que cambian el modelo obligatorio, quedan mezcladas con las de producto. La dimensión caso de la base debe ampliarse con LUGAR, EDIF, ANIMAL y OBJ antes de clasificar.

texto: ### 6.1 Vocabulario

encabezado: AI Production Director › 6. Reglas de resolución de conflictos › 6.1 Vocabulario
texto: El vocabulario prohibido de `video`/dramaturgy (+ `aurora-prompt-linter` si está) **gana siempre**: "cinematic", "epic", "stunning", "masterpiece", "beautiful lighting", "professional", "high quality", emociones nombradas sin cuerpo. Esto **anula explícitamente** la regla de `ai-video-storyboard` de cerrar cada prompt con "cinematic 1080p, synchronized audio". En su lugar: la resolución, aspect ratio, duración y si el modelo genera audio se especifican como parámetros técnicos concretos según el archivo del modelo destino.

texto: ### 6.2 Sintaxis de modelo

encabezado: AI Production Director › 6. Reglas de resolución de conflictos › 6.2 Sintaxis de modelo
texto: `ai-video-storyboard` pide prompts model-agnostic; `video`/`image` (smixs) existen para sintaxis por modelo. Resolución: model-agnostic SOLO en artefactos intermedios (storyboard, shot cards). Todo prompt FINAL se escribe en la sintaxis del modelo destino según el archivo smixs correspondiente. Si el modelo no tiene archivo smixs (p.ej. Flux, Midjourney, Ideogram), la autoridad es el adaptador de `visual-prompt-forge`.

texto: ### 6.4 División forge ↔ smixs

texto: # Output format

encabezado: Output format
texto: When you return the prompt, structure it like this:

encabezado: Output format
texto:
```
Model: <nano-banana-2 | nano-banana-pro | gpt-image-2>
Quality: <low | medium | high>          (only for gpt-image-2)
Size / Ratio: <e.g. 1536×1024 or 16:9>

Prompt:
<the prompt text, ready to copy>

Notes:
- <anything you inferred or assumed because the user did not specify>
```

encabezado: Output format
texto: For edits, also include an explicit preserve-list (mandatory for gpt-image-2, recommended for nano-banana):

encabezado: Output format
texto:
```
Change: <one concrete thing>
Preserve: <face, pose, lighting, framing, geometry, ...>
Constraints: <no extra objects, no drift, ...>
```

texto: # Final response style

encabezado: Final response style
texto: Prefer: ready-to-copy prompts, hex colors, concrete materials, named compositions, model-specific syntax (5-slot for GPT Image, natural prose for Nano Banana).

encabezado: Final response style
texto: Avoid: tag soup ("cool, modern, 4k"), vague praise ("stunning, epic, masterpiece" — actively hurts GPT Image 2), negative framing ("no people, no cars" — invert to positive), external comparisons ("like Apple ad" — describe the visual properties instead), numerical lens parameters in Nano Banana prompts (it ignores them).

encabezado: Image Editing
texto: Универсальные паттерны. Логика edit'а различается по моделям:

encabezado: Image Editing
texto: - **GPT Image 2:** двухколоночная логика **Change / Preserve / Constraints**. Preserve list повторять каждую итерацию, иначе drift. Опционально `mask_image_url` для точечных edit'ов. Лучшая identity preservation. См. [gpt-image.md](gpt-image.md#editing--двухколоночная-логика).

encabezado: Image Editing

encabezado: Golden Rules
texto: # Golden Rules

encabezado: Golden Rules
texto:
Универсальные принципы. Работают для **обеих** семей моделей (Nano Banana и GPT Image 2).
Для модельной специфики см. [nano-banana.md](nano-banana.md), [gpt-image.md](gpt-image.md).

encabezado: Golden Rules › 1. Start with a Verb
texto: ## 1. Start with a Verb

encabezado: Golden Rules › 1. Start with a Verb
texto: Tell the model the primary operation: "Create", "Generate", "Design", "Transform", "Convert", "Edit". This sets the intent before details.

encabezado: Golden Rules › 2. Positive Framing
texto: ## 2. Positive Framing

encabezado: Golden Rules › 2. Positive Framing
texto: Describe what you WANT, not what you don't want. The model understands presence better than absence.

encabezado: Golden Rules › 2. Positive Framing
texto: - ✅ "empty street" → ❌ "street with no cars"

encabezado: Golden Rules › 2. Positive Framing
texto: - ✅ "clean background" → ❌ "no clutter"

encabezado: Golden Rules › 2. Positive Framing
texto: - ✅ "solo portrait" → ❌ "no other people"

encabezado: Golden Rules › 3. Edit, Don't Re-roll
texto: ## 3. Edit, Don't Re-roll

encabezado: Golden Rules › 3. Edit, Don't Re-roll
texto: Image 80% correct? Request specific change:

encabezado: Golden Rules › 3. Edit, Don't Re-roll
texto: - "Change lighting to sunset"

encabezado: Golden Rules › 3. Edit, Don't Re-roll
texto: - "Make text neon blue"

encabezado: Golden Rules › 3. Edit, Don't Re-roll
texto: - "Move chart to right third"

encabezado: Golden Rules › 4. Natural Language
texto: ## 4. Natural Language

encabezado: Golden Rules › 4. Natural Language
texto:
❌ Bad: "Cool car, neon, city, night, 8k"
✅ Good: "A cinematic wide shot of a futuristic sports car speeding through a rainy Tokyo street at night. Neon signs reflect off wet pavement and metallic chassis."

encabezado: Golden Rules › 5. Be Specific
texto: ## 5. Be Specific

encabezado: Golden Rules › 5. Be Specific
texto: | Element | Vague | Specific |

encabezado: Golden Rules › 5. Be Specific
Golden Rules › 5. Be Specific
texto: | Subject | "a woman" | "sophisticated elderly woman in vintage Chanel-style suit" |

encabezado: Golden Rules › 5. Be Specific
texto: | Material | "shiny" | "brushed steel with matte finish" |

encabezado: Golden Rules › 5. Be Specific
texto: | Color | "dark green" | "#0d3d2d deep emerald" |

encabezado: Golden Rules › 5. Be Specific
texto: | Position | "on the right" | "right third, bleeding off edge" |

encabezado: Golden Rules › 6. Provide Context
texto: ## 6. Provide Context

encabezado: Golden Rules › 6. Provide Context
texto: Context helps model make logical decisions:

encabezado: Golden Rules › 6. Provide Context
texto: - "for Brazilian gourmet cookbook" → infers professional plating, shallow DOF

encabezado: Golden Rules › 6. Provide Context
texto: - "for executive strategy presentation" → infers corporate aesthetic

encabezado: Golden Rules › 6. Provide Context
texto: - "for children's educational app" → infers friendly, colorful style

encabezado: Golden Rules › 7. Quote Text Exactly
texto: ## 7. Quote Text Exactly

encabezado: Golden Rules › 7. Quote Text Exactly
texto: Any text for rendering goes in quotes:

encabezado: Golden Rules › 7. Quote Text Exactly
texto: - "[HEADLINE TEXT]"

encabezado: Golden Rules › 7. Quote Text Exactly
texto: - Labels: "[Revenue Growth]", "[Net Income]"

encabezado: Golden Rules › 7. Quote Text Exactly
texto: - Specify weight: bold, thin, extra bold

encabezado: Golden Rules › 7. Quote Text Exactly
texto: - Specify position: "upper third", "centered"

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors
texto: ## World Knowledge Anchors

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors
texto: GPT Image 2 обладает глубокими знаниями о культуре, эпохах и визуальных стилях. Вместо описания каждой детали — дай модели культурный/временной/жанровый якорь, и она сама заполнит аутентичные детали.

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: ### Три типа якорей

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: **Era anchors** — временной и географический маркер, который вызывает целый визуальный мир:

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Bethel, NY, August 1969" → Woodstock aesthetic без необходимости описывать тай-дай, грязь, сцены

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Berlin, November 1989" → падение стены, толпы, граффити, эйфория

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Tokyo, 1982" → неоновый Shinjuku, аналоговая электроника, ранний cyberpunk

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: **Cultural anchors** — перенос визуального языка одного культурного объекта на другой контекст:

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "{game_title} in {real_city}" → автоматически применяет визуальный стиль игры к реальной локации (GTA style, Persona style, и т.д.)

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Soviet constructivism poster about {modern_topic}" → стиль Родченко/Эль Лисицкого на современную тему

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Ukiyo-e print of {modern_scene}" → японская гравюра с современным содержанием

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: **Genre anchors** — режиссёр/фотограф/движение как линза:

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Peter Lindbergh influence" → сильный Ч/Б, минимальная ретушь, raw editorial

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Wes Anderson palette" → симметричный кадр, пастельная палитра, центрированная композиция

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Studio Ghibli mood" → мягкое акварельное небо, зелёная листва, тёплый ностальгический свет

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Roger Deakins lighting" → натуральный свет, глубокие тени, кинематографичный объём

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Правила использования
texto: ### Правила использования

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Правила использования
texto: 1. **Используй как HIGH-LEVEL steering** — якорь задаёт настроение и эстетику, а не заменяет весь промпт

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Правила использования
texto: 2. **Комбинируй с конкретными визуальными деталями** — якорь устанавливает мир, детали устанавливают специфику

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Правила использования
texto: 3. **Не стакай несколько genre anchors** — выбери один. "Peter Lindbergh + Wes Anderson" = каша

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Правила использования
texto: 4. **Era/cultural anchors работают лучше с GPT Image 2** (world knowledge). С Nano Banana результат менее предсказуем — NB больше опирается на явные описания

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Примеры
texto: ### Примеры

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Примеры
texto: **Era anchor + конкретные детали:**

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Примеры
texto:
```
Create an editorial portrait set in Havana, 1957.

Subject: jazz musician leaning against pastel-colored colonial building,
holding trumpet loosely at his side. Linen suit, open collar.
Lighting: harsh Caribbean afternoon sun, deep shadows under awning.
Format: 3:4
```

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Примеры
texto: > "Havana, 1957" вызывает: старые американские машины на заднем плане, облупившаяся штукатурка, кованые балконы, тропическая атмосфера — без необходимости это описывать.

texto: GPT Image 2 сильнее всего реагирует на разделение по секциям. Пиши лейблами, не сплошным текстом.

texto: # Multi-Panel Compositions

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions
texto: Single-image layouts containing multiple frames, panels, or grid cells. Unlike [storyboards.md](storyboards.md) (sequential images generated one-at-a-time), these patterns produce **one image** with all panels baked in.

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions
texto: Core principle: explicitly number and describe every panel. Models need panel-by-panel instructions — vague requests like "show multiple angles" produce inconsistent grids.

texto: ## 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid
texto: **When to use:** Same person shown from 4 angles/crops in one image for an editorial or casting look.

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid › Template (5-slot format)
texto: ### Template (5-slot format)

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid › Template (5-slot format)
texto:
```
Scene: 2x2 grid of four editorial portraits, minimal gap between panels. {background_description}. {lighting_style}.

Subject: {subject_description} — same person in all four panels, consistent identity and wardrobe.

Important Details:
Top-left: front-facing portrait, direct eye contact, shoulders up
Top-right: extreme macro close-up of face — eyes, skin texture, freckles visible
Bottom-left: lower angle looking up, chin slightly raised, confident expression
Bottom-right: side profile, clean silhouette against background

Consistent lighting across all four panels. Skin texture realistic, no airbrushing.

Use Case: editorial photography, model portfolio, casting composite
Constraints: same person in every panel, no wardrobe changes between panels, no extra people, no text overlays
```

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - Omitting which quadrant gets which angle — model arranges arbitrarily

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid › Template (5-slot format)

texto: ## 3. 3-Panel Campaign Collage

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 3. 3-Panel Campaign Collage
texto: **When to use:** Hero shot + close-up + action for a campaign visual — horizontal or vertical triptych.

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 3. 3-Panel Campaign Collage › Template (5-slot format)
texto: ### Template (5-slot format)

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 3. 3-Panel Campaign Collage › Template (5-slot format)
texto:
```
Scene: Three-panel {orientation} collage for {brand_name} campaign. Panels separated by thin white lines.

Subject: {model_description} showcasing {product_description}.

Important Details:
Panel 1 (left/top): Hero wide shot — full figure of model with product, environmental context, lifestyle setting
Panel 2 (center/middle): Close-up product detail — {product_detail_description}, tactile textures, sharp focus
Panel 3 (right/bottom): Action shot — model using/wearing/interacting with product, candid energy, slight motion blur on extremities

Consistent warm golden-hour lighting across all panels. Same model identity throughout.
{typography_instruction}

Use Case: social media campaign visual, brand lookbook
Constraints: same person across all panels, consistent color grading, no stock-photo stiffness, {product_name} must be visible in every panel
```

Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence
texto: ## 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence
texto: **When to use:** Fashion editorial or film-style sequence — multiple camera angles of the same scene in one image.

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto: ### Template (5-slot format)

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto:
```
Scene: 6-frame cinematic sequence arranged in a 3x2 grid. Dark film-strip aesthetic with thin black borders. {location_description}.

Subject: {subject_description}, wearing {wardrobe_description}. Same person, same outfit, same location across all 6 frames.

Important Details:
Frame 1 (top-left): Top-down bird's eye view — subject seen from directly above, full body visible against ground/floor
Frame 2 (top-center): Low angle looking up — subject towering over camera, dramatic perspective, sky/ceiling visible
Frame 3 (top-right): Wide isolation shot — subject small in frame, vast environment dominates, sense of scale
Frame 4 (bottom-left): Close-up with slight tilt — face and upper body, Dutch angle, intimate intensity
Frame 5 (bottom-center): Motion frame — subject mid-action ({motion_action}), natural motion blur on limbs
Frame 6 (bottom-right): Grounded final — medium shot, subject at rest, direct gaze, resolving the sequence

Photographer reference: {photographer_style}
Lighting: consistent {lighting_description} across all frames

Use Case: fashion editorial, film lookbook, director's shot list visualization
Constraints: same person and wardrobe in every frame, no costume changes, consistent color grading, no text overlays
```

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto: **Variables:**

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{subject_description}` — model details

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{wardrobe_description}` — clothing

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{location_description}` — setting

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{motion_action}` — what the motion frame captures (e.g., "walking forward", "turning sharply", "jumping")

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{photographer_style}` — (e.g., "Peter Lindbergh desaturated realism", "Helmut Newton dramatic contrast")

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{lighting_description}` — (e.g., "overcast natural light, soft shadows")

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto:
**Recommended size:** 1536x1024 (landscape, 3x2 grid)
**Model:** GPT Image 2 `quality: medium` or Nano Banana Pro
**Common pitfalls:**

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - Not naming each frame explicitly — "various angles" is too vague, the model needs per-frame instructions

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - Top-down and low-angle in the same grid confuse the model if you don't anchor each frame to a grid position

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - Motion blur instruction must be specific ("blur on hands and feet") or the model applies blur everywhere

Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster
texto: ## 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster
texto: **When to use:** Full narrative in one image — 3x4 grid (3 columns, 4 rows) for animation or video pre-production.

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster › Template (5-slot format)
texto: ### Template (5-slot format)

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster › Template (5-slot format)
texto:
```
Scene: 12-panel storyboard poster, 3 columns x 4 rows. Dark background with each panel in a clean rectangular frame. "{title}" in bold white text at the top of the image. Below each panel: scene number and one-line description in small white text.

Subject: {character_description} — maintain consistent character design, proportions, and colors across all 12 panels.

Important Details:
Panel 1: {scene_1} — "{caption_1}"
Panel 2: {scene_2} — "{caption_2}"
Panel 3: {scene_3} — "{caption_3}"
Panel 4: {scene_4} — "{caption_4}"
Panel 5: {scene_5} — "{caption_5}"
Panel 6: {scene_6} — "{caption_6}"
Panel 7: {scene_7} — "{caption_7}"
Panel 8: {scene_8} — "{caption_8}"
Panel 9: {scene_9} — "{caption_9}"
Panel 10: {scene_10} — "{caption_10}"
Panel 11: {scene_11} — "{caption_11}"
Panel 12: {scene_12} — "{caption_12}"

Panels read left-to-right, top-to-bottom (like a comic page). Character appearance, clothing, and color palette must stay identical across all 12 panels — only pose, expression, angle, and environment change.

Style: {art_style}

Use Case: animation pre-production, pitch deck visualization, narrative overview poster
Constraints: all 12 panels must be distinct scenes (no duplicates), character consistency is critical, scene numbers must be legible, {language} captions
Quality: high
```

texto: **Variables:**

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{title}` — project/episode title displayed at top

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{character_description}` — detailed character design (colors, outfit, distinguishing features)

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{scene_1}` through `{scene_12}` — visual description of each panel

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{caption_1}` through `{caption_12}` — text label under each panel

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{art_style}` — (e.g., "Pixar-style 3D", "anime cel shading", "watercolor illustration", "graphic novel ink")

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{language}` — caption language

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster › Template (5-slot format)
texto:
**Recommended size:** 1024x1536 (portrait — 3 columns x 4 rows needs vertical space)
**Model:** GPT Image 2 `quality: high` (text-heavy — scene numbers and captions must be readable)
**Common pitfalls:**

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - Character drift is the biggest risk at 12 panels — repeat character design details in the prompt, not just "same character"

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster › Template (5-slot format)

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster › Template (5-slot format)

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - Art style must be stated once and applied uniformly; mixing styles across panels produces visual chaos

texto: ## General Multi-Panel Tips

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
texto: **Panel count vs. detail trade-off:** More panels = less detail per panel. 4 panels allow rich per-panel descriptions; 12 panels need brief, visually distinct descriptions (3-8 words each).

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
texto: **Subject consistency:** Always include an explicit instruction: "same person / same character / same product across all panels." Repeat key identity markers (hair color, clothing, distinguishing features) rather than saying "same as before."

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
texto: **Grid specification:** Always state the grid dimensions (e.g., "3x2 grid, 3 columns 2 rows"). Saying "6 panels" without layout instruction lets the model choose an unpredictable arrangement.

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
texto: **Borders and gaps:** Be explicit — "thin white border between panels" or "borderless, no gaps." Default behavior varies by model and is unreliable.

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
texto: **Reading order:** State it: "left-to-right, top-to-bottom" or "numbered 1-9 starting top-left." Without this, narrative flow may be jumbled.

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
texto: **Model selection summary:**

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
texto: - Text/labels in panels --> GPT Image 2 `quality: high`

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
texto: - Budget/exploration --> Nano Banana 2 or GPT Image 2 `quality: low`

encabezado: Character Design Patterns › Character Turnaround Sheet (3-View)

```

Subject: {character_name} — {character_description} — shown in three views arranged left to right: front view (facing camera), three-quarter side view (turned 75 degrees right), back view (facing away)

Use Case: game character pre-production, animation model sheet, 3D reference handoff
Constraints: no background elements, no props in hands, no dramatic poses — neutral standing pose only, all three views must depict the exact same character with identical outfit and proportions, no drop shadows, no gradient backgrounds
```

texto: ## City Across Two Centuries (Time-Split Composition)

encabezado: Poster & Illustration Patterns › City Across Two Centuries (Time-Split Composition)
texto: Use for urban development campaigns, anniversary materials, cultural exhibitions, or editorial features — a single city view divided down the middle, one half historical and one half modern.

encabezado: Poster & Illustration Patterns › City Across Two Centuries (Time-Split Composition)
texto: <!-- Source concept: time-split composition — same city view, two eras side by side -->

encabezado: Poster & Illustration Patterns › City Across Two Centuries (Time-Split Composition)
texto:
```
Scene: wide establishing shot of {city_landmark_view}, frame divided vertically down the center — left half shows the scene in {historical_era}, right half shows {modern_era}
Subject: the same geographic viewpoint across two time periods, architecture and infrastructure transforming at the dividing line
Important Details:
  Left half ({historical_era}): {historical_details} — muted {historical_palette} palette, {historical_atmosphere}, period-accurate architecture, {historical_figures} going about daily life, {historical_transport}
  Right half ({modern_era}): {modern_details} — {modern_palette} palette, {modern_atmosphere}, contemporary architecture where old buildings once stood (some landmarks preserved), {modern_figures}, {modern_transport}
  Dividing line: not a hard cut — elements morph and blend across a narrow 5% transition zone (a horse-drawn cart becomes a car, a gas lamp becomes LED, cobblestones become asphalt, a tree grows taller)
  Sky transitions too: {historical_sky} on left to {modern_sky} on right
  Camera angle: elevated three-quarter view (roughly 30 degrees above street level) to show depth of both eras
Use Case: city anniversary campaign, urban development feature, cultural exhibition poster, editorial illustration
Constraints: both halves must depict the SAME geographic location (matching terrain, river, hill positions), transition zone should feel organic not pasted, scale and perspective consistent across both halves, no text unless specified, no anachronistic elements (modern items in historical half or vice versa outside the transition)
```

encabezado: UI Mockups & Social Media Patterns › Personal Color Analysis Board
texto: ## Personal Color Analysis Board

encabezado: UI Mockups & Social Media Patterns › Personal Color Analysis Board
texto: Use to create a visual color analysis graphic from a portrait — seasonal palette classification, clothing color comparisons, and accessory recommendations in an organized layout.

encabezado: UI Mockups & Social Media Patterns › Personal Color Analysis Board
texto: <!-- Source concept: personal color analysis / seasonal color palette board with side-by-side comparisons -->

encabezado: UI Mockups & Social Media Patterns › Personal Color Analysis Board
texto:
```
Scene: white background, organized multi-section layout with thin #E0E0E0 divider lines, clean editorial formatting
Subject: personal color analysis board for {subject_description}
Important Details:
  Section 1 — Portrait & Season (top, full width): {subject_description} portrait photo (head and shoulders, natural lighting, neutral expression) on the left. To the right: season classification "{season_type}" in medium bold text, with a 4x3 grid of small color swatches showing the {num_palette} best colors for this season type ({palette_colors}), each swatch labeled with its name in tiny text below
  Section 2 — Clothing Comparison (middle): two side-by-side panels. Left panel "{good_label}": the subject wearing a top in {flattering_color} — skin looks healthy, face appears lifted and bright. Right panel "{bad_label}": the same subject wearing a top in {unflattering_color} — skin appears washed out or sallow. Small caption under each explaining the effect in 5-8 words
  Section 3 — Recommendations (bottom): horizontal strip with {num_recs} small squares — each showing a recommended item ({rec_items}) in one of the palette colors, with a one-word label below (e.g. "Scarf", "Blazer", "Lipstick", "Frames")
  Visual-first design — images and swatches dominate, text is short labels only
  Clean editorial feel, no decorative flourishes
Use Case: personal styling consultation, color analysis service deliverable, fashion content
Constraints: same person in all panels showing the subject, swatches must be solid flat color (no gradients), labels are short (1-3 words max), no paragraphs of body text, layout must feel organized and scannable, no overlapping sections
```

encabezado: UI Mockups & Social Media Patterns › Personal Color Analysis Board
texto: **Key levers:** `{subject_description}` (age, skin tone, hair color, eye color — needed for accurate seasonal analysis), `{season_type}` (Warm Spring, Cool Summer, Warm Autumn, Cool Winter — or sub-seasons like Soft Autumn, Bright Winter), `{palette_colors}` (12 hex values matching the season, e.g. Warm Autumn: rust #B7410E, olive #708238, mustard #E1AD01, burgundy #722F37...), `{num_palette}` (12), `{flattering_color}` / `{unflattering_color}` (specific colors with hex), `{good_label}` / `{bad_label}` (e.g. "Warm Coral" / "Cool Pink"), `{num_recs}` (4-6), `{rec_items}` (scarf in olive, blazer in navy, lipstick in warm rose, eyeglass frames in tortoise)

encabezado: UI Mockups & Social Media Patterns › Personal Color Analysis Board
texto: **Recommended model:** GPT Image 2 (`quality: high`) — color accuracy of palette swatches is critical, plus small text labels throughout

texto: # Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis
texto: Use this reference when the user asks to analyze an image and convert it to a generation prompt: **style transfer**, **mood reference**, **"сделай промпт по этой картинке"**, **"перенеси стиль/образ"**, **"проанализируй кадр"**, **"image to prompt"**, **"reverse-engineer this look"**.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis
texto: You become a **professional Vision Agent**. Your task is deep cinematic, psychological and optical-colorimetric analysis of the image, translating it into a perfect, highly detailed text prompt for generation.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis
texto: The process has two strict steps. Do not skip Step 1. Do not freestyle Step 2.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis
Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: ## STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: Scan the image as **raw data** and extract facts based on:

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: - **Cinematic composition** — Bruce Block's visual structure

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: - **Color theory** — Itten

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: - **Perceptual psychology** — Arnheim

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: - **Directing references** — Spielberg / Scorsese / Tarantino

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: - **Cinematography & colorimetry** — Valentin Zheleznyakov

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: Evaluate the following four parameter blocks.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
texto: ### 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
texto: - **Who / What:** precise clothing (era, style, materials), age, skin texture, makeup / toning, micro-expressions.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
texto: - **Shot size (after Mascelli):** Extreme Long Shot (ELS), Long Shot, Medium Shot, Two-shot / Three-shot, Close-Up (CU), Choker CU, Extreme CU, Insert shot.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
texto: - **Directing & force placement (Blocking after Kenworthy):** isolating the character at the edge of the frame (anxiety), physical barriers, face turned away from camera, shooting from behind (effect of unknown / powerlessness). Height difference (Level Change) for dominance.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
texto: - **Kinetics & perceptual forces (Arnheim):** visual weight of the object, center of gravity. Internal tension of form (compression / stretching / twisting). Pose, plasticity, motion vectors. Imitation of swift action (motion blur) or monumental stillness.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
texto: - **Color and emotion (Itten):** psychological impact of the local color of the subject.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
texto: - **Gaze:** direction, eyeline anchor, interaction with the frame edges, look into the lens.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
texto: ### 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
texto: - **Setting & Art Direction:** place, era, background, architecture, specifics of materials and surface textures (gloss, matte, rust).

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
texto: - **Three-plane depth (Spielberg):** clear separation into Foreground (with leading details), Midground (action plane), Background.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
texto: - **Figure & ground (Arnheim):** degree of subject isolation, overlapping of forms, mass relationships. Use of reflections (mirrors, windows) to expand context.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
texto: - **Tonal & aerial perspective (Zheleznyakov):** drop in contrast, desaturation, washing out, shift toward cool (blue-cyan) tones in the background.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
texto: - **Frame geometry:** structural framework (axes of symmetry / asymmetry), claustrophobic compression, surface divisions. Illusion of depth via Foreground framing.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 3. Lighting — chiaroscuro, color and contrast
texto: ### 3. Lighting — chiaroscuro, color and contrast

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 3. Lighting — chiaroscuro, color and contrast
texto: - **Optical & visual contrast (Zheleznyakov):** ratio of lit and shadow areas (OVK). Depth and density of shadows. Exact local color vs. color modified by lighting (valeurs).

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 3. Lighting — chiaroscuro, color and contrast
texto: - **Lighting scheme:** Key, Fill, Backlight / Rim, Modeling. Rembrandt lighting, Chiaroscuro. Height, hardness (Hard / Soft) and type of source.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 3. Lighting — chiaroscuro, color and contrast
texto: - **Broken light & reflexes (Zheleznyakov):** use of shadow masks (gobos), light through blinds / foliage, color reflexes from neighboring objects onto skin / clothing.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 3. Lighting — chiaroscuro, color and contrast
texto: - **Tonality & color:** light key (High-key / Low-key). Threshold Silhouette. Itten's 7 contrasts. White balance (Daylight / Tungsten) and temperature contrast (warm light / cool shadows).

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 4. Tech & Cinematography — optics, filters and film texture
texto: ### 4. Tech & Cinematography — optics, filters and film texture

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 4. Tech & Cinematography — optics, filters and film texture
texto: - **Camera (angles & viewpoint):** Angle (High angle, Low angle, Eye-level, Dutch tilt). Objective camera, Subjective, POV, Over-the-shoulder (OTS). Movement imitation (Push-in, Tracking shot).

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 4. Tech & Cinematography — optics, filters and film texture
texto: - **Optics & DOF:** Focal length (wide-angle for distortion / coverage, telephoto for spatial compression). Depth of field. Rack focus, bokeh.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 4. Tech & Cinematography — optics, filters and film texture
texto: - **Optical filters & attachments (Zheleznyakov):** diffusion filters (Pro-Mist, Black Pro-Mist, Fog, Double Fog, Low Contrast) for highlight bloom (halation), skin softening, lowering of micro-contrast. Polarizers (cutting reflections).

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 4. Tech & Cinematography — optics, filters and film texture
texto: - **Effects & texture:** Frame format (70mm, 35mm, IMAX). Exposure (motion blur). Stylization (Bleach Bypass). Film Grain, chromatic aberration.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 4. Tech & Cinematography — optics, filters and film texture
Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 2 — PROMPT SYNTHESIS
texto: ## STEP 2 — PROMPT SYNTHESIS

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 2 — PROMPT SYNTHESIS
texto: Assemble the final prompt from Step 1 data.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 2 — PROMPT SYNTHESIS
texto: Rules:

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 2 — PROMPT SYNTHESIS
texto: - Write **only keywords separated by commas, in English**.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 2 — PROMPT SYNTHESIS
texto: - Describe **strictly what you see**. Do not invent new objects.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 2 — PROMPT SYNTHESIS
texto: - **No filler.** Never write "The image shows...", "A picture of...", "I can see...".

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 2 — PROMPT SYNTHESIS
texto: - **Strict word order** (this formula is non-negotiable):

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 2 — PROMPT SYNTHESIS
texto:
```
[Shot type, optics and angle], [Subject, mise-en-scène / blocking, visual weight, clothing and action], [Multi-plane environment (Foreground / Midground / Background), overlapping and geometry], [Lighting scheme, optical contrast, gobos and reflexes], [Color palette, temperature contrast and aerial perspective], [Color Grading, diffusion filters, film stock, textural artifacts]
```

texto: ### Negative-space-aware composition

encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Negative-space-aware composition
texto: When a shot has on-screen text, the **shot subject must reserve space for it**. This is enforced at storyboard time, not generation time.

encabezado: On-Screen Text › Composition rules › Negative-space-aware composition
texto:
If text is in the right third → subject composition leaves the right third clear.
If text is lower third → subject upper two-thirds.
If text is centered → subject framed to negative space around center.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 1. What an animatic keyframe must do
texto: ## 1. What an animatic keyframe must do

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 1. What an animatic keyframe must do
texto: In an animatic the **panel is the unit, not the shot.** A shot has duration, motion, and sound to carry its function across time. A keyframe has one frozen image and must carry the same function in a single glance. So every panel does four things at once, in one still:

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 1. What an animatic keyframe must do
texto: - **One readable story-beat** — name it in one sentence before generating. If you cannot, the panel is not ready (`dramaturgy.md` §1).

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 1. What an animatic keyframe must do
texto: - **One function tag** — Establish / Reveal / Power / Pressure / Detail / Reaction / Shift / Impact / Aftermath / Exit (`role-modes.md` §4). The tag is the question the panel answers. In a faceless spot **Reaction** is reassigned from a human face to the *machine's* face — the needle jumping, the slick wrinkling, the nose squatting. Treat gauges and rubber as the actor.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 1. What an animatic keyframe must do
texto: - **One emotion** — routed through metal, rubber, light, or anatomy, never named (`dramaturgy.md` §2). Mixed signals = no signal.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 1. What an animatic keyframe must do
texto: - **One implied motion** — the movement the still cannot perform, frozen as its physical residue (§4).

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 1. What an animatic keyframe must do
texto: A panel that carries a beat, a function, an emotion, and an implied motion earns its place. A panel missing any of the four is a *fantik* — wrapper without candy (`dramaturgy.md` §3). The discipline of this whole file is: **you cannot prompt "motion" or "emotion" into a still — you prompt the physical consequence each leaves behind.**

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 1. What an animatic keyframe must do
Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 2. The keyframe card
texto: ## 2. The keyframe card

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 2. The keyframe card
texto: The shot card in `dramaturgy.md` §11 describes a moving shot. A keyframe needs a *still*-specific card: every field describes a frozen image, and three fields are new (implied camera, emotion-via-object, motion-rendered-as-still). Fill every field before generating. Empty fields reveal missing direction.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 2. The keyframe card
texto:
```text
KEYFRAME CARD
- Panel ID.            01, 02, 03
- Timecode.            on-screen life in the animatic (e.g. 0:10.5, HOLD 2s)
- Function tag.        Establish / Reveal / Power / Pressure / Detail /
                       Reaction / Shift / Impact / Aftermath / Exit
- Beat.                what changes in the story in this one still
- Framing + lens.      ECU / CU / MCU / wide / macro insert / POV + lens token
                       (24mm immersive ... 100mm macro — camera-lighting-vocabulary.md §3)
- Subject / anchor.    the ONE object or anatomy the eye lands on in 0.3s
- Depth layers.        FG job (frame / obstruct / put us inside)
                       MG job (the subject / the act)
                       BG job (stakes / context / rival)
- Implied camera.      the move this still is the first frame OF
                       (push-in, whip, bumper-POV, joust) — what it would do if it ran
- Light + palette.     one motivated source + direction + the surface it rims;
                       concrete colors, amber-ban repeated
- Emotion-via-object.  the feeling a face would show, mapped to an object's state (§5)
- Motion-as-still.     which frozen cue carries the missing movement (§4):
                       smear / partial blur / streak / vector / sharp-blur / held stillness
- Caption / label.     one word: setup / commitment / mistake / recovery /
                       proof-of-speed / result
- Sound.               what audio sits under the held frame, where the cut bites
                       (fill even though it is a still — dramaturgy.md §11)
- Production note.      prop, rig, continuity anchor
```

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 2. The keyframe card
texto: The card maps straight onto format C: `Function`, `Framing`, `Implied camera`, `Light`, `Sound`, `Emotion-via-object` become the table columns. The three still-specific fields — **implied camera, emotion-via-object, motion-as-still** — are the ones a normal shot card does not force you to name, and they are exactly the ones that keep a panel from going flat.

texto: ## 4. Composing a still that reads as MOTION

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 4. Composing a still that reads as MOTION
texto: A keyframe cannot ramp, cut, or whip. Each missing move resolves into one of **six frozen cues**. Never write "motion" — write the artifact motion leaves behind. State the cue in the card's *Motion-as-still* field and again in the prompt's camera/light clause; models default to over-clean stabilization and will sand the speed off unless told (§7).

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 4. Composing a still that reads as MOTION
texto: Per-technique kit (triad + the still application):

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 4. Composing a still that reads as MOTION
texto: - **Frozen motion blur** — what it does to emotion: differential blur reads as velocity made tactile, the world torn past a steady subject — where seen: Dod Mantle whip-panned every overtake in *Rush* so the background dissolves. — *in a keyframe* [Shift/Impact]: hero car tack-sharp, entire background raked into horizontal streaks, foreground objects elongated into light-rods. The most powerful single-panel speed trick: **sharp hero + fully smeared world.** Equal blur everywhere = soft photo; differential blur = speed.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 4. Composing a still that reads as MOTION
texto: - **Tyre wrinkle / partial blur** — emotion: physics you can feel, force arrested at its peak — seen: Goodyear's deliberately silent slow-mo of the slick sidewall folding; Ritchie's speed-ramp as the exclamation mark. — *in a keyframe* [Detail/Reaction]: macro into the rear sidewall, the wrinkle caught at its deepest fold, smoke just blooming at the contact patch, everything else crisp. One arrested ten-thousandth of a second. The hero detail to *hold*.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 4. Composing a still that reads as MOTION
texto: - **Smoke / debris / spray shape** — emotion: force given a visible body, dread made airborne — seen: NHRA burnout-cam, "a wall of smoke" backlit at ground level. — *in a keyframe* [Pressure/Power]: backlit tyre smoke as a luminous wall (front-lit smoke is dead gray nothing); water-box spray frozen as a constellation of specular droplets, each rimmed on its leading edge. Atmosphere only reads when light passes through it (§5).

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 4. Composing a still that reads as MOTION
texto: - **Posture / lean vector** — emotion: a stillness that can only resolve forward; the eye does the launching — seen: Vaughn's charged poses (*Kingsman*, *Layer Cake*) — every frame loaded with a trajectory. — *in a keyframe* [Power/Shift]: **no neutral panels.** Car at idle = front wheels micro-lifting, body slung onto the rear axle. Hand on wheel = fingers mid-clench. Compose the negative space *ahead* of the subject, the direction it is about to fire into.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 4. Composing a still that reads as MOTION
texto: - **Leading lines / light streak** — emotion: a rail for the eye that also encodes direction and speed — seen: Papamichael's asphalt-in-frame (*Ford v Ferrari*), the road as the speedometer. — *in a keyframe* [Power/Impact]: lane centerline raking to a vanishing point, sodium/mercury practicals smeared as long reflections down wet asphalt. Keep the texture (chevrons, tar seams, rubber marks) so the streak has something to streak.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 4. Composing a still that reads as MOTION
texto: - **Off-balance dutch** — emotion: imbalance, loss of grip, threat — seen: Raimi's canted attack frames (*Evil Dead II*). — *in a keyframe* [Impact]: cant the horizon hard at the one loss-of-traction beat — tyre breaking away, car stepping sideways. Reserve it for a single instability beat so it stays loud; dutch as wallpaper reads as bad framing.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 4. Composing a still that reads as MOTION
texto: **The speed-budget rule** (from the race-truth school): a still sells velocity when **at least three of five coexist in one frame** — (a) camera at/below bumper height, (b) asphalt streaking the lower frame, (c) a near foreground reference passing the edge, (d) sharp hero against motion-blurred background, (e) a mechanical-vibration cue (trembling mirror, doubled needle, smeared rim). One cue is a car photo. Three is velocity. If a "fast" panel cannot name three, reframe lower, drag the camera to the asphalt, throw a cone or barrier into the foreground.

Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 5. Emotion without faces in a still
texto: ## 5. Emotion without faces in a still

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 5. Emotion without faces in a still
texto: A face does four jobs: shows the feeling, shows where it looks, shows the cost, shows the decision. Faces banned, redistribute: **decision → anatomy mid-action; internal state → an object crossing a threshold; looking/rivalry → space** (§6 and `dramaturgy.md` §2). Assign one job per panel and tag it. The emotion must already be frozen *inside the object* — a still cannot let motion blur do the emotional work for it.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 5. Emotion without faces in a still
texto: Two load-bearing rules:

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 5. Emotion without faces in a still
texto: - **Anatomy only on a decision.** A hand at rest is filler; a hand *deciding* is a shot. Before drawing any hand/foot panel, name the verb — grip / latch / shift / preload / release. No verb, no panel. Render tendons raised, glove leather creasing, one hard side-light carving knuckle texture, the rest in shadow (Leone's hands-before-the-draw; Nike *Take It to the Next Level*, first-person, no hero face).

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 5. Emotion without faces in a still
texto: - **Objects only when they change state.** A static gear-lever says "car stuff" and flatlines. Board the **after** state of a threshold-crossing; the before is implied (Honda *Cog*: every object does something irreversible). Tach pinned in the red, not idling. Ignition lamp blooming live, not dark. Slick caught mid-fold.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 5. Emotion without faces in a still
texto: Use the substitution table as the core deliverable — when the script wants an emotion and no face is available, render this object at this crop. Cold palette throughout.

Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
texto: ## 6. The loaded frame for one panel

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
texto: A keyframe is a diagram the viewer solves in 0.3s and re-reads with pleasure at 1s. With no face, the geometry and the depth stack do the acting.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
texto: > **Core law of the loaded panel.** One focal point, one emotion, three working depth layers, zero dead objects. Answer one question in the first glance; reward a second look.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
texto: **Depth-layer jobs (FG / MG / BG).** Write the prompt in three explicit depth clauses, each with a stated job. This is the engine of "reads in one glance, rewards a second" (extends `dramaturgy.md` §10 into a single still). If all three planes carry the same blur or scale, you have one plane, not three — force a sharp MG subject against a soft FG frame and a soft BG stake (shallow DOF is the panel's hierarchy tool, `camera-lighting-vocabulary.md` §3).

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
texto: | Plane | Default job | Drag-race objects | Function it serves |

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
texto: | **Foreground** | frame / obstruct / put us inside | roll-cage bar, mirror edge, harness strap, smoke wisp, wet glass | Pressure, Power |

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
texto: | **Midground** | the subject / the act | hand on shifter, knuckles on wheel, foot on pedal, tach face | Detail, Shift, Impact |

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
texto: | **Background** | stakes / context / rival | staging bulb, rival lane headlight, finish line, narrowing barrier | Establish, Reveal, Pressure |

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
texto: **One-glance + reward** — what it does to emotion: an instantly readable frame creates trust; a frame that rewards re-reading creates density and worth. With no face to anchor on, a muddy panel collapses to nothing. — *in a keyframe*: name the single focal point before generating (tach needle / staging bulb / knuckle), put it on a strong line, demote everything else to support. The second-look reward is a reflection, a bridge object, or a state indicator — one, not a clutter.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
texto: **Centerline spine, then break symmetry** — emotion: a single dominant axis (lane stripe, the Christmas Tree, a dividing wall) gives the eye a rail and makes even a chaotic frame readable; breaking it the instant one car noses ahead reads as momentum. — seen: Anderson centers for instant legibility; Bong breaks balanced staging to show a power shift. — *in a keyframe*: build one head-on symmetric "breath" panel — both cars mirrored across the centerline, Tree dead-middle, equal negative space (tag **Establish/Pressure**, hold longest). On the next panel, break the mirror — hero a nose ahead, rival shoved soft, centerline slid off the third (tag **Shift/Impact**). Use the pair exactly once, at the launch; overusing symmetry kills the speed.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
texto: **Functional vs decorative clutter — the evidence test.** Keep an object only if it does at least one of: (1) **indicator of state** (replaces the face — tach in the red, white knuckles), (2) **stage of action** (advances the beat — front wheel 7" off the line = pre-stage), (3) **bridge to the next panel** (sets up a match-cut or a reach). Dead detail — coffee cup, mirror dice, dashboard sticker — shows no state, advances nothing, bridges nowhere. Cut it. "Each object is a clue" (Park); functional clutter *loads* the frame, decorative clutter *weakens* it.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel
texto: **Angle encodes the beat** (no face, so the angle *is* the emotion): low / ground-level = power, threat, launch force (**Power, Impact**); eye-level lateral = parity, rivalry stated (**Establish**); high / top-down = judgment, smallness, aftermath (**Aftermath, Exit**).

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 6. The loaded frame for one panel

texto: ## 7. From keyframe to image-gen prompt

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 7. From keyframe to image-gen prompt
texto: A keyframe card becomes a still prompt by following the universal skeleton (`universal-rules.md` U1) with weight at the start (U2). **Lead with framing + lens + light + palette + anchor object** — these are the load-bearing tokens for a still; the model puts most attention on the first 30-40% of tokens.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 7. From keyframe to image-gen prompt
texto: Panel → prompt skeleton:

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 7. From keyframe to image-gen prompt
texto:
```text
[Framing + lens]           e.g. "Low bumper-height macro, 24mm, shot past a blurred roll-cage bar"
[Anchor subject + state]   the ONE object at its threshold: "rear slick sidewall wrinkling at the contact patch"
[Depth clauses, 3 jobs]    FG frame / obstruct · MG subject / act · BG stake / rival
[Motion-as-still cue]      "sharp subject against horizontal motion-blurred background, foreground reference elongated into a light-streak, rear rim spokes smeared to a disc"
[Light + palette]          one motivated source + direction + surface it rims; concrete colors; amber-ban
[Texture]                  "fine film grain heaviest in shadow, halation on the practicals, one anamorphic flare, crushed blacks"
[Face rule]                "no face" — or "driver a featureless silhouette against blown rival headlights, only knuckle highlights legible"
[Aspect / no-speed-up note]  "no speed-ramp; build velocity into the static frame"
```

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 7. From keyframe to image-gen prompt
texto: Rules that keep the still honest:

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 7. From keyframe to image-gen prompt
texto: - **Name the differential blur explicitly.** Models default to over-clean stabilization. Write "motion blur on background, fast-shutter look, sharp subject, rim spokes smeared to a disc." Equal/no blur is the most-faked and most-failed cue (anti-fake firewall, §4 speed-budget).

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 7. From keyframe to image-gen prompt
texto: - **Keep faces out or fragmented.** Convert any would-be face to silhouette / contre-jour with a rim and one glint. No features.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 7. From keyframe to image-gen prompt
texto: - **Render audio as physical consequence, never as a named sound.** "Loud engine" is banned filler (`dramaturgy.md` §2) — prompt "heat-haze warp off the headers, exhaust flame, chassis squat, sidewall wrinkle" instead.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 7. From keyframe to image-gen prompt
texto: - **Anti-sterile guard.** If the panel could be captioned "clean," "beautiful lighting," or "high quality," it has failed — name the grain, the bloom, the crushed black, the one specular hit (`universal-rules.md` U12). One motivated source dominates; ~70% of the frame stays unlit (`camera-lighting-vocabulary.md` §5-7).

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 7. From keyframe to image-gen prompt
texto: Cross-link the vocabulary file for every framing/lens/light token. Then **the keyframe is the locked first frame**; hand it to `seedance.md` / `kling.md` / `veo.md` with the single dominant move (one per 5s — `camera-lighting-vocabulary.md` §2) to animate it. Name in the model syntax: "low bumper-height camera, asphalt streaking, motion blur on background, sharp subject, no speed-up."

texto: ## 9. Checklist: does this keyframe earn its place

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 9. Checklist: does this keyframe earn its place
texto: Run before every panel ships. Drop the panel if it fails.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 9. Checklist: does this keyframe earn its place
texto: - [ ] **Function tag named.** One of Establish / Reveal / Power / Pressure / Detail / Reaction / Shift / Impact / Aftermath / Exit. No tag → drop it.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 9. Checklist: does this keyframe earn its place
texto: - [ ] **One readable beat**, sayable in one sentence. If you cannot caption it (setup / commitment / mistake / recovery / proof-of-speed / result), it is a *fantik* — drop it.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 9. Checklist: does this keyframe earn its place
texto: - [ ] **Emotion-via-object** present — the feeling a face would carry, frozen in a knuckle / needle / pedal / smoke / sweat-bead (§5). No state-change, no emotion → drop it.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 9. Checklist: does this keyframe earn its place
texto: - [ ] **Speed or drama cue** present — ≥1 of the six motion-as-still cues (smear / partial blur / streak / vector / sharp-blur / held stillness), or a deliberate held-still pause. "Fast" panels carry ≥3 of the five speed cues (§4).

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 9. Checklist: does this keyframe earn its place
texto: - [ ] **State-change, not static fetish** — the object crosses a threshold (idle→flare, clean→smoked, planted→lifting). No idle anatomy, no parked gear-lever.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 9. Checklist: does this keyframe earn its place
texto: - [ ] **Three depth layers**, each with a stated job (FG frame/obstruct, MG subject, BG stake). One focal point; every other object is evidence, not decoration.

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 9. Checklist: does this keyframe earn its place
texto: - [ ] **Implied camera named** — the move this still is the first frame of, physically mountable on the car (no god-angle render).

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 9. Checklist: does this keyframe earn its place
texto: - [ ] **Cold palette held** — steel/cyan/magenta/mercury-white, red and green as accents only, amber ≤15% and point-source (toxic, never cozy). One motivated source, ~70% unlit, one hard specular hit. Texture named (grain, halation, one flare), not "clean."

encabezado: Keyframes for an animatic (opornye kadry) › 9. Checklist: does this keyframe earn its place
texto: - [ ] **No face**, or a face fragmented past usefulness (silhouette / reflection only).
