texto: ## 3. Selling speed in a single frame

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 3. Selling speed in a single frame
texto: A still has no engine note and zero motion. It sells velocity through the **speed-budget rule** — a frame reads fast only when **≥3 of five cues coexist** (camera at/below bumper height · asphalt streaking the lower frame · a near foreground reference passing the edge · sharp hero against motion-blurred background · a mechanical-vibration cue). The full rule, with the anti-fake firewall, lives in `animatic-keyframes.md` §4; do not re-derive it. One cue is a car photo; three is velocity; five and even a parked car reads dangerous. If a "fast" panel can't name three, reframe lower, drag the camera to the asphalt, throw a barrier into the foreground.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 3. Selling speed in a single frame
texto: Two race-domain extensions the general file does not carry:

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 3. Selling speed in a single frame
texto: **The foreground reference catalog** (cue *c*, the cheapest and strongest speed multiplier). Place the reference *near the lens* (so it smears most) and *passing the edge* (so it reads as transiting, not parked). Keep one near object tack-sharp so the brain measures the smear against it.

Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces
texto: ## 7. Light & color for speed without faces

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces
texto: Faces are banned, so light is the only actor left. It does not "set a mood" — it **rims a material** so a piece of metal, rubber or skin reports the emotion a face would. General light grammar (sources, direction, quality) is `camera-lighting-vocabulary.md` §4–7; the anti-sterile firewall is `animatic-keyframes.md` §7 + `universal-rules.md` U12. The race-specific governing law: *embrace the dark* (crush blacks, ~70% of the frame unlit), *one motivated practical per panel* (Tree lamp, headlight, sodium lamp, brake glow), *light is specular not ambient* (every panel needs ≥1 hard specular hit — no specular, no information).

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: - **Hard key on the working hand** [Detail/Pressure]: single hard source 45° camera-side onto knuckles on the shifter — finger shadows rake the skin, sweat reads as discrete specular dots, veins as ridges, background crushed. The whitening knuckle IS the fear.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: - **Backlight / rim on metal edge** [Power]: hard white or cyan source behind/above at low angle drawing one bright line down the roof gutter, mirror housing or wing edge; body in shadow, only the contour glows, against black sky.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: - **Backlit smoke** [Pressure/Establish]: hard cyan or mercury-white punching *through* tire smoke from behind; volumetric shafts, the car a dark mass dissolving into glowing haze, red tail-light bleed inside the smoke for the danger accent. Front-lit smoke is dead gray nothing — always rim it from behind.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: - **Brake-disc glow** [Detail/Impact]: macro on the wheel, glowing orange-red rotor through the spokes as the *only* warm element (toxic heat), rim the caliper and spokes with that glow, everything else steel blue — the one ember in a cold frame.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: - **Specular on wet asphalt — the mirror** [Establish/Shift]: low bumper-height, lane stretching away, practicals (Tree, sodium lamps, headlights) reflected as long vertical smears down the wet surface as the composition's spine; pull the real lamps half out of frame, keep the mirror. Wet asphalt at night = `dramaturgy.md` §9 guilt/threat, and the cheapest way to put more cold light in frame without lifting blacks.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: - **Silhouette / contre-jour** [Power/Pressure]: helmet/shoulder as pure black shape against a blown headlight or the Tree's amber bank, one thin rim defining the form plus one glint on the visor edge, no features. The brain fills the dark with something worse than any face.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: - **The Christmas Tree as the scene's lamp and clock** [Pressure→Impact]: put the Tree bank in frame as the dominant practical — its glow the only key. Stage 1: two blue bulbs as cold points in the lacquer. Stage 2: three ambers blazing, amber-as-toxin spill on wet asphalt, held. Stage 3: green pops, a single green reflection streaks the hood. Match-cut the round bulb → round headlight → round tach.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: **Texture and atmosphere.** Name the grain, never "clean": fine-to-medium film grain (heaviest in shadow), halation/bloom on hard practicals (soft glow ring + hard hot core), one anamorphic flare off the dominant source, slight chromatic fringe on the hottest edges (anti-sterile test in `animatic-keyframes.md` §7). One atmospheric pressure per panel (`dramaturgy.md` §9, Kurosawa) — backlit tire smoke, frozen launch grit lit on its leading edge, heat-haze warping the rimmed edge, wet asphalt as the mirror. Don't stack smoke + haze + spray in one still or it turns to mud. Keep Tony Scott's restlessness and grain; discard his warm grade.

Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: ## 10. Anti-fake guard

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: The race-specific list of panels that kill credibility — do not draw. (The general per-panel earns-its-place checklist is `animatic-keyframes.md` §9; run that on every panel as well.)

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No high, clean, "beauty" god-angle for action beats — drop to bumper height; low/wide/close beats polish.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No perfectly stable cabin — render visible vibration (trembling mirror, doubled needle, smeared rim); tilt 1–3°.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No long-lens speed panel without road texture or a passing reference object.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No panel that only works "when sped up" — build the speed into the static composition (squat, lifted nose, slick wrinkle).

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No air around the car on a speed beat — crowd the near edge with barrier/rival/wall.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No sharp wheel rim on a moving car — smear the spokes into a disc.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No shiny-bodywork beauty pass — shoot force transmission (tire load, chassis squat, exhaust flame).

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No warm cozy grade — cold palette, red as danger accent only, amber ≤15% and toxic (§7).

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No banned panel: static fetish insert (lever/badge/wheel with no verb, no state-change); anatomy at rest; a detail you cannot caption with a §4 label; all-proof-of-speed board with no commitment/mistake/recovery; decorative dashboard clutter (keyring, dice, coffee cup — "each object is a clue"); warm wash without narrative function.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: Before sending the board, run `animatic-keyframes.md` §9 (per-panel master checklist), `dramaturgy.md` §15 and `universal-rules.md` §13 over it. The most-violated step is the three-detail check — do not skip it.

---
name: visual-asset-critic
description: Critique a generated image against its source storyboard shot and prompt, producing revision notes. Use when the user has generated an image and wants feedback before committing. Triggers on "does this match the brief", "review this render", "is this on-brand", "what should I change", or uploading an image alongside a shot ID. The QA loop for AI visuals. Works even without a storyboard-architect run. Pairs with storyboard-architect upstream, visual-prompt-forge sibling.
---

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic
texto: # Visual Asset Critic

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic
texto: You are the editorial second-eye on AI-generated images. Most teams don't have one, they generate, glance, accept, and ship. This skill is the structured review pass that catches what a tired creator misses.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic
texto: The output is a critique with concrete, actionable revision notes. Not vibes. Not "looks good." Specific, prompt-level or post-level fixes.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › When to use
texto: ## When to use

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › When to use
texto: Trigger when the user:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › When to use
texto: - Uploads or links a generated image with a question about quality

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › When to use
texto: - Asks "does this match the storyboard"

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › When to use
texto: - Says "review this render", "is this on-brand", "what should I change"

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › When to use
texto: - Has a generated image and a `shots.json` shot reference and wants QA

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › When to use
texto: - Has a generated image and just wants editorial feedback (no storyboard reference)

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › What you produce
texto: ## What you produce

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › What you produce
texto: **Two artifacts from every review, always both:** a human-readable markdown critique (the primary surface) and a machine-readable critique JSON (so a pipeline can gate on the verdict instead of parsing prose). The JSON is detailed in Step 6; it never replaces the markdown.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › What you produce
texto:
The JSON goes to `output/critiques/round-{N}/{shot_id}.critique.json`. One file per shot
per round, never a shared filename. A 12-shot project reviewed over three rounds writes 36
critiques; when they all went to `output/critique.json` it kept one, and which one depended
on review order.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › What you produce
texto: The markdown critique uses these sections:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › What you produce
texto:
```
## Verdict
ACCEPT / REVISE / REJECT, one line

## What's working
2–4 specific positives. Concrete observations, not flattery.

## What's not working
2–5 specific issues. Each one cites a layer. Brand Lock, Series Lock, Shot Spec, Composition, Technical, or Continuity.

## Revision plan
For each issue, the fix:
- Prompt-level (re-roll with this change to the prompt)
- Post-level (acceptable to address in editing/compositing)
- Re-roll required (no prompt fix; budget 2–3 attempts)

## Confidence
HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW, how sure you are about the verdict
```

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: ## Inputs

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: You need:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: | Input | Required? | Default if absent |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: | The generated image | Yes | Cannot critique without it |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: | Shot ID + shots.json | Recommended | If absent, ask for shot intent in a sentence |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: | brand-lock.snapshot.md | Recommended | If absent, critique only on technical merits |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: | The original prompt used | Helpful | If absent, infer from intent |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: If only the image is provided with no context, ask for one piece of information: **what was this shot supposed to be?** A single sentence is enough to anchor the critique.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow
texto: ## Workflow

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent
texto: ### Step 1. Establish intent

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent
texto: What was this shot supposed to do? Pull from:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent
texto: - Shot's `rationale` field (if shots.json provided)

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent
texto: - Shot's `subject`, `framing`, `angle`, `motion` fields

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent
texto: - User's stated intent (if no shots.json)

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent
texto: - The beat this shot serves

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent
texto: If you can't establish intent in one sentence, ask. Don't critique blind.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: ### Step 2. Critique by layer

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: Read `references/critique-rubric.md` for the full rubric. Quick version, check the image against:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: 1. **Brand Lock**, does it respect palette, mood, "never" list?

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: 2. **Series Lock**, does it match character/environment/lighting anchors?

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: 3. **Shot Spec**, does framing/angle/composition match the spec?

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: 4. **Composition**, does it reserve space for on-screen text if applicable?

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: 5. **Technical**, skin texture, hands, eyes, anatomy, AI artifacts?

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: 6. **Continuity**, if previous shots in the series are available, does it match?

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: For each layer, note: pass / soft fail / hard fail. The verdict aggregates these.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: ### Step 3. Map issues to fixes

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: For every "not working" point, the critique must say what to do about it. Three buckets:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: **Prompt-level fix**, change the prompt and re-roll. Specify the exact change:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: > "The character has brown hair instead of salt-and-pepper. Add 'salt-and-pepper hair' verbatim from series_lock to the prompt, it's missing in the current prompt."

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: **Post-level fix**, acceptable to address in compositing. Specify what:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: > "Color grade is slightly cool, push warmth +5 in post, no need to re-generate."

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: **Re-roll required**, no prompt fix will help; the generator just produced a bad sample. Budget 2–3 attempts:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: > "Hands are mangled. This is a known Flux failure mode; re-roll 2–3 times with same prompt and pick the best."

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict
texto: ### Step 4. Verdict

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict
texto: | Verdict | When |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict
Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict
texto: | ACCEPT | All layers pass or soft-fail in ways post can fix |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict
texto: | REVISE | One or two layers hard-fail; clear fix path |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict
texto: | REJECT | Three+ layers fail or one critical layer (Brand Lock, Series Lock) hard-fails with no clear fix |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
texto: ### Step 5. Confidence

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
texto: Be honest about uncertainty:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
texto: | Confidence | When |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
texto: | HIGH | Storyboard reference + brand-lock + prompt all available, clear assessment |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
texto: | MEDIUM | Some references missing but core intent is clear |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
texto: | LOW | Only the image, intent is inferred; verdict is your best guess |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
texto:
HIGH is a factual claim about what you had, not a mood. `tools/validate_critique.py`
rejects a `1.1` critique that claims HIGH while `shot_id`, `brand_lock_ref`, or
`prompt_ref` is null, because that combination says the three inputs HIGH depends on were
not there.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: ### Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto:
After writing the markdown critique, **also** write
`output/critiques/round-{N}/{shot_id}.critique.json` conforming to
`templates/critique.schema.json` at version `1.1`. Same review, two surfaces. The markdown
is for the human; the JSON is so an automated QA loop (e.g. `visual-prompt-forge` revision
mode) can act on the verdict without parsing prose.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: **Map the markdown to the schema, section for section:**

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | Markdown | JSON field |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `## Verdict` | `verdict` (`ACCEPT` / `REVISE` / `REJECT`) |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `## What's working` bullets | `working[]` (one string each) |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `## What's not working` + `## Revision plan` | `issues[]`, merge them: each issue carries its layer/note from "what's not working" and its `fix_type`/`fix` from the matching revision-plan line |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `## Confidence` | `confidence` (`HIGH` / `MEDIUM` / `LOW`) |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto:
**Provenance, all of it required at 1.1.** A verdict is a claim about specific bytes. Name
them, and hash them:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | Field | Value |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `run_id`, `round` | from `run.json` and the round directory you are writing into |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `created_at` | UTC instant, `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ` |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `shot_id` | the shot, or `null` for a standalone image with no storyboard |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `image_ref`, `image_sha256` | the frame you reviewed, and its SHA-256 |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `prompt_ref`, `prompt_sha256` | the prompt file it came from, and its SHA-256 |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `brand_lock_ref`, `brand_lock_sha256` | the snapshot you judged against, and its SHA-256 |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `generator`, `model_version` | the generator id from `_capabilities.json`, and its model version |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `seed` | if the generator exposes one, else `null` |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto:
```bash
shasum -a 256 output/frames/round-1/shot_03.png \
              output/prompts/round-1/flux.txt \
              output/brand-lock.snapshot.md
```

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto:
Every one of those fields is required, and every one is nullable. That combination is
deliberate: `null` records that an input genuinely was not available, while a missing field
records nothing at all. If you did not have the prompt, write `prompt_ref: null` and drop
your confidence to MEDIUM. Do not omit the key.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto:
The hashes are the point. Without `image_sha256`, a frame regenerated after this review
still satisfies `image_ref`, and a stale ACCEPT sails through the gate attached to a file
nobody looked at.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: **Severity, assign one per issue.** This is the field the gate runs on, so map it from the layer rubric deterministically:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | Severity | Means | Maps from |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `minor` | soft-fail, fixable in post | a soft-fail on any layer; `fix_type: post-level` |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `major` | hard-fail **with** a clear fix path | a hard-fail that a prompt change or re-roll fixes |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `blocking` | hard-fail on a critical layer (Brand Lock / Series Lock) with **no** clear fix, or a defect that makes the asset unusable | an unrecoverable hard-fail |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: **Gating rule, the verdict is derived from severities, not chosen freely.** This guarantees the markdown verdict and the JSON verdict always agree:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: - Any `blocking` issue ⇒ verdict is `REJECT`.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: - Three or more `major` issues ⇒ verdict is `REJECT`.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: - One or two `major` issues (and no blocking) ⇒ verdict is `REVISE`.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: - Only `minor` issues, or none ⇒ verdict is `ACCEPT` (with post notes).

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto:
The three-major rule used to read "escalate to REJECT at your discretion." Discretion in a
gate is not a gate, and it disagreed with `references/critique-rubric.md`, which called
three hard fails a REJECT outright. It is now a threshold, and the validator enforces it.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: Pick the markdown `## Verdict` by this same rule.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate
texto: ### Step 7. Run the gate

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate
texto: Writing a schema-valid critique is not the same as passing the gate. Run it:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate
texto:
```bash
python tools/validate_critique.py output/critiques/round-1/shot_03.critique.json
```

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate
texto:
Or check the whole tree at once, which also recomputes every hash against the files on
disk:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate
texto:
```bash
python tools/validate_provenance.py output/
```

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate
texto:
This step is not optional and it is not someone else's job. A critique that says `ACCEPT`
while carrying a `major` issue is a bug, and the only reason to write a validator for that
bug is to actually run it. Before this step existed, the gate ran in CI against two
fixtures that ship in the repo and never once against a real client's critique.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate
texto:
Worked examples: `examples/critique.accept.json` and `examples/critique.revise.json` show
the shape at version `1.0`, which is still valid and carries no provenance.
`examples/worked-run/critiques/` shows version `1.1` with real hashes, two shots across two
rounds.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules
texto: ## Hard rules

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 1. No vibes-based critique
texto: ### Rule 1. No vibes-based critique

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 1. No vibes-based critique
texto: "Looks great" / "feels off" without specifics is not a critique. Every observation must reference something in the image (composition, color, anatomy, lighting direction, etc.).

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 2. Prompt-level fixes must be specific
texto: ### Rule 2. Prompt-level fixes must be specific

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 2. Prompt-level fixes must be specific
texto: "Change the prompt" is not a fix. "Add 'salt-and-pepper hair' to the character anchor, it's currently missing" is a fix.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 3. Don't critique what wasn't asked
texto: ### Rule 3. Don't critique what wasn't asked

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 3. Don't critique what wasn't asked
texto: If the brief was "founder at laptop, calm mood" and the generation delivered exactly that, don't note that "the room could be more visually interesting." That's scope creep, not critique.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 4. Be honest about generator limits
texto: ### Rule 4. Be honest about generator limits

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 4. Be honest about generator limits
texto: Some failures (mangled hands, weird eye reflections, jewelry shimmer) are known generator weaknesses. Surface them as such, don't pretend a different prompt will fix them. Recommend re-roll or post.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 5. When in doubt, ACCEPT and recommend post
texto: ### Rule 5. When in doubt, ACCEPT and recommend post

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 5. When in doubt, ACCEPT and recommend post
texto: Generation is one stage in a pipeline. If the image is 80% right and the gap is fixable in post, that's an ACCEPT with post notes. Don't send the user back to re-generate when an editor would handle it in 90 seconds.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Reference
texto: ## Reference

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Reference
texto: - `references/critique-rubric.md`, the full layer-by-layer rubric

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Example output
texto: ## Example output

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Example output
texto:
> ## Verdict
> REVISE
>
> ## What's working
> - Composition correctly reserves the right two-thirds for text overlay (matches shot_03 rationale)
> - Lighting direction matches series_lock (window-left, warm afternoon)
> - Mood reads as calm/considered, on-brand
>
> ## What's not working
> - **Series Lock, character mismatch.** The character has brown hair, but series_lock specifies "salt-and-pepper." This is a verbatim-anchor failure.
> - **Technical, left hand.** Hand on the laptop has six fingers (Flux known failure mode).
> - **Shot Spec, framing.** Generated as MS but spec called for MCU. Subject is too small in frame.
>
> ## Revision plan
> - **Hair:** Prompt-level. Add "salt-and-pepper hair" to the character anchor in the prompt, currently missing. Re-roll.
> - **Hand:** Re-roll required. Generate 2–3 more times with same prompt and pick a clean one.
> - **Framing:** Prompt-level. Change "medium shot" to "medium close-up" in the prompt. Re-roll.
>
> ## Confidence
> HIGH

encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
texto: ## From pass/fail to severity

encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
texto:
The tables above grade each check as pass, soft fail, or hard fail. The JSON critique
records a severity instead, and the verdict is derived from those severities. Map them
this way, and only this way:

encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
texto: | Rubric result | Severity | Why |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
texto: | Soft fail on any layer | `minor` | Post can absorb it. `fix_type` is usually `post-level` |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
texto: | Hard fail **with** a clear fix path | `major` | A prompt change or a re-roll resolves it |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
texto: | Hard fail on Brand Lock or Series Lock **with no** fix path | `blocking` | Nothing downstream recovers this |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
texto: | Any defect that makes the asset unusable | `blocking` | Same, regardless of layer |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto: ## Aggregating verdict

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto: The verdict follows from the severities. It is not a separate judgement:

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto: | Severities present | Verdict |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto: | any `blocking` | REJECT |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto: | three or more `major` | REJECT |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto: | one or two `major` | REVISE |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto: | only `minor`, or none | ACCEPT (with post notes) |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto:
`tools/validate_critique.py` enforces exactly this table, so a critique that disagrees with
it fails rather than shipping. Earlier versions of this file counted hard fails and called
3+ a REJECT while the skill said "escalate at your discretion." Those two rules disagreed,
and the disagreement is the reason the threshold is now a number.

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto:
Soft fails are noted but don't change the verdict on their own. If you have three or more of
them, look again: a cluster of soft fails usually means one of them is really a hard fail
you talked yourself out of.

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember
texto: ## Speed bumps to remember

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember
texto: - **Don't critique what wasn't asked**, if the spec didn't call for cinematic mood, don't say "could be more cinematic"

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember
texto: - **Don't pile-on once verdict is set**, if you're rejecting, list the issues that drive the rejection; don't list every cosmetic concern

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember
texto: - **Be specific, always**, "lighting is off" is not a critique; "key light is camera-right but series_lock says camera-left" is

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember
texto: - **Cite the layer**, every issue gets tagged with which layer it falls under. This makes the fix path obvious

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember
texto: - **Distinguish prompt failure from generator failure**, if the prompt was fine and the generator produced garbage hands, that's "re-roll required", not "fix the prompt"

```markdown
## Composición básica

### Regla de tercios
- Divide el encuadre en una retícula de 3×3
- Coloca el sujeto en los puntos de intersección
- Sitúa el horizonte en la línea superior o inferior

### Líneas guía
- Usa líneas para conducir la mirada
- Caminos, ríos, barandales
- Que apunten al sujeto

### Encuadre dentro del encuadre
- Enmarca al sujeto con elementos del primer plano
- Marcos de puerta, ventanas, ramas
- Aporta capas y profundidad

### Simetría y equilibrio
- Simetría perfecta = estabilidad, solemnidad
- Asimetría = dinamismo, tensión
- Equilibra el peso visual

### Espacio negativo
- El vacío refuerza el punto focal
- Da "espacio para respirar" al sujeto
- Estética minimalista
```

Each image generator rewards a different prompting style, short and high-signal for Midjourney, natural-language for Flux, paragraph-form for GPT Image, text-aware for Ideogram. A prompt that crushes in one will produce slop in another.

texto: Every prompt is composed from these layers. Read `references/prompt-anatomy.md` for the full theory. Quick version:

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters
texto: Each adapter file documents the prompting style, parameter syntax, and known pitfalls for that generator. You **must** read the adapter before writing prompts for it. Don't guess from training data, image-gen syntax has churned multiple times.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters
texto: **`adapters/_capabilities.json` is the single source of truth for per-generator limits** (`max_prompt_words`, `supports_text_render`, `supports_motion`, `aspect_param`, and so on). Read it once at the start and respect those values when composing, and do not target motion on a stills-only generator.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters
texto:
`max_prompt_words` is a ceiling. The range in an adapter `.md` is the recommended target
and always sits inside that ceiling, so a `.md` saying "40 to 70 words" under a ceiling of
120 is guidance, not a conflict. Where a fact in a `.md` and a fact in the JSON genuinely
disagree, **the JSON wins**.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters
texto:
That rule is now enforced rather than trusted. `tools/validate_capabilities.py` fails the
build when an adapter advertises more words than its ceiling, or when an adapter never
documents the `aspect_param` the JSON tells you to send. The second check exists because
nano-banana's matrix entry said `aspect_ratio` while its adapter said the API expects
`aspectRatio`; the precedence rule meant the wrong one won, silently, on every prompt.

The `#` lines are comments; the user copies just the prompt body. `tools/copy-prompt.py`
parses this format, treating a comment line that names a shot as a block header and any
other comment inside a block as an annotation it will not copy.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4. Write output files

Record the run and round in the header, not a wall-clock "Generated" line. A timestamp in
the header made every file differ between two otherwise identical runs, which is a strange
thing to put in an artifact whose selling point is determinism.

it covers.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop)
texto: ## Revision mode (closing the QA loop)

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop)
texto: This is what `visual-asset-critic`'s structured output is for. When the user hands you `shots.json` plus one or more `critique.json` files (the machine-readable verdict the critic writes), don't re-forge the whole storyboard, re-emit prompts for **only the shots that failed**, with the fix already applied.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Trigger
texto: ### Trigger

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Trigger
texto: The user says "apply the critique", "revise the failed shots", "re-roll what didn't pass", or hands over an output tree containing `critiques/`.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto: ### Workflow

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto:
1. Read every critique under `output/critiques/round-{N}/`, where N is the highest round
   present. Each file is one shot's verdict (`shot_id`, `verdict`, `issues[]`).

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto: 2. Skip any with `verdict: ACCEPT`. Those are done.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto:
3. **Stop on `REJECT`.** A REJECT means the critic found a blocking issue, or three or more
   major ones: a failure with no clear fix path. Re-emitting a prompt for it pretends
   otherwise. List the rejected shots, say what the critic said about them, and ask the
   user how to proceed. Common answers are a change to the shot spec, a change to the
   brand-lock, or a different generator, and all three are decisions above this skill's
   pay grade.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto: 4. For every `REVISE` shot, walk its `issues[]` and branch on `fix_type`:

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto:
- **`prompt-level`**, recompose that shot's prompt with the change in `fix` applied
     (e.g. add the missing series_lock anchor). Re-emit it.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto:
- **`re-roll`**, keep the prompt identical; the generation was just a bad sample.
     Re-emit it with a `# fix [Technical, re-roll]` annotation saying to take 2-3 samples
     and pick the cleanest.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto:
- **`post-level`**, do **not** re-emit. The fix happens in compositing, not a new
     generation.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto:
5. A shot whose issues are all `post-level` needs no new prompt. Leave it out of the
   revised file and add its id to `post_only_shots` on the new round entry in `run.json`.
   Saying it in chat is not recording it: that obligation has to exist on disk or the
   compositing step is a memory.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto: 6. Re-apply the five-layer anatomy and the same adapter as the original run.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Output
texto: ### Output

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Output
texto:
Write `output/prompts/round-{N+1}/revised-{generator}.txt` containing only the revised
shots, then append the round to `run.json`. Annotate each shot with what changed and why,
citing the issue:

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Output
texto:
```
# shot_03, reframe, 11.0-16.0s, MCU eye-level push, revision (was REVISE)
# fix [Series Lock, major]: added 'salt-and-pepper hair' to the character anchor (was missing)
# fix [Shot Spec, minor]: medium shot -> medium close-up
{the revised prompt}
```

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Output
texto:
The block header leads with the shot id, same as a full pass. `tools/copy-prompt.py`
identifies a block by the shot id near the start of the line, so a header that led with
"Revision of" produced a file the paste helper could not read at all, which is
inconvenient in the one file the operator is about to paste from repeatedly.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Output
texto:
Tell the user which shots were revised, which need only post work, which were rejected,
and which were already ACCEPT. Then they generate the revised shots and run
`visual-asset-critic` again.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Determinism, and its limits
texto: ### Determinism, and its limits

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Determinism, and its limits
texto:
Given the same `shots.json`, the same brand-lock, and the same critique, this should
produce the same revised prompt. Nothing in the file format fights that any more: no
wall-clock stamps, no random ordering.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Determinism, and its limits
texto:
What the format cannot guarantee is the judgement in between. Applying a `fix` field means
reading a sentence of English and editing prose, so hold yourself to the narrowest edit
that satisfies the fix and leave every other layer byte-identical. If you find yourself
rewriting a prompt the critique did not ask you to touch, stop: that is drift, and it will
read as a mystery six shots later.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules
texto: ## Hard rules

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules
texto: These are non-negotiable. Violating them produces broken output even if the prompt looks fine.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 1. Text is never in the prompt
texto: ### Rule 1. Text is never in the prompt

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 1. Text is never in the prompt
texto: If the shot has `on_screen_text: "text_03"`, the prompt does NOT contain the text content. Text is composited separately. The only exception: Ideogram, where text-in-image is the reason you'd choose it, but even then, treat it as an explicit override flagged in rationale.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 2. Brand colors never in shot subject prose
texto: ### Rule 2. Brand colors never in shot subject prose

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 2. Brand colors never in shot subject prose
texto: Colors come from the series_lock color_grade and the brand_lock palette. They get rendered into the prompt by the adapter. Don't write "deep navy blazer" in the shot subject if "deep navy" is already in the palette, that's a duplicated description and produces oversaturation.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto: ### Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto:
The series_lock `environment`, `lighting`, and `color_grade` strings flow into every
prompt **verbatim**. This is what produces visual consistency across shots. If you
paraphrase or vary, shots stop matching each other.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto:
Verbatim means the whole string, unedited. Not "the same idea in better prose". The
failure mode is specific and easy to walk into: you are writing fluent descriptive
English, `environment` is "minimalist home office, white walls, oak desk, single
houseplant", and it reads more naturally as "a minimal home office with white walls and
an oak desk". That is drift. The frames stop matching, and it stays invisible until you
line up six shots and see six different rooms.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto:
Capitalising the first letter to start a sentence is fine, because the check is
case-insensitive. "Minimalist home office, white walls, oak desk, single houseplant."
satisfies the rule and reads like a sentence. Nothing else may change: no reordering, no
dropped clause, no synonym, no inserted adjective.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto:
`character` is a warning rather than an error, because a shot with no person in it can
legitimately leave it out. When the shot has a person, it is verbatim too.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto: This rule is enforced now, not trusted:

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto:
```bash
python tools/validate_prompts.py output/
```

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto:
It exists because a careful authoring pass over a seven-shot storyboard drifted on these
anchors in all seven shots while every other validator stayed green.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 4. Adapters are the source of truth on syntax
texto: ### Rule 4. Adapters are the source of truth on syntax

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 4. Adapters are the source of truth on syntax
texto: If your training data says Midjourney uses `--style 4a` and the adapter file says `--style raw`, the adapter wins. Image-gen syntax changes monthly. The adapter is current; your training is not.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: ### Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: A prompt can be beautifully written and still be impossible to shoot. Every prompt declares, before anything else:

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: - **Where the body sits in frame.** Which third it occupies. On a piece that composites two eras with a vertical mask, a body sitting on the centre line gets split in half and no amount of post fixes it. This is the single most expensive failure in the kit, and it is invisible until the mask goes on.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: - **The point of view.** Profile, frontal, side, rear. "A man walking" is not a shot.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: - **The direction of travel.** Left to right, right to left, toward camera. Without it the generator picks, and consecutive shots stop matching.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: - **Nothing that contradicts the camera.** A subject who walks away from camera cannot also keep the same size in frame.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: - **Handedness in any two-person contact.** If one raises a hand, name which one, or you get two right hands meeting.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: - **No brand marks.** Logos and lettering are composited in post. Generators deform them.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 5. Prompts must be reproducible
texto: ### Rule 5. Prompts must be reproducible

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 5. Prompts must be reproducible
texto: Every prompt is composed from the same inputs the same way. If two consecutive runs produce different prompts for the same shot, the skill is broken. Determinism is the whole point.

texto: ## Pitfalls to avoid

encabezado: Adapter: GPT Image (1.5 / 2) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't write Midjourney-style comma stacks**. GPT Image parses them as a list of disconnected concepts

encabezado: Adapter: GPT Image (1.5 / 2) › Pitfalls to avoid

encabezado: Adapter: GPT Image (1.5 / 2) › Pitfalls to avoid

encabezado: Adapter: GPT Image (1.5 / 2) › Pitfalls to avoid

encabezado: Consistency Locks
texto: # Consistency Locks

encabezado: Consistency Locks
texto: Visual consistency across a storyboard is the hardest problem in AI image generation. Generators are stateless, every prompt is interpreted fresh. Without consistency locks, shot 1 and shot 7 will look like different productions.

encabezado: Consistency Locks
texto: This document covers the techniques that actually work in 2026.

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 1. Verbatim character anchors
texto: ## Lock 1. Verbatim character anchors

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 1. Verbatim character anchors
texto: The most effective single technique. The character is described in `series_lock.character` once, and that exact string appears in every shot's prompt verbatim. No paraphrasing, no synonyms, no "improvement."

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 1. Verbatim character anchors
texto: **Good (consistent):**

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 1. Verbatim character anchors
texto:
```
shot_01: "founder, mid-thirties, salt-and-pepper hair, navy crewneck, stubble"
shot_02: "founder, mid-thirties, salt-and-pepper hair, navy crewneck, stubble"
shot_07: "founder, mid-thirties, salt-and-pepper hair, navy crewneck, stubble"
```

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 1. Verbatim character anchors
texto: **Bad (inconsistent):**

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 1. Verbatim character anchors
texto:
```
shot_01: "a thoughtful entrepreneur in his thirties, dark hair, casual sweater"
shot_02: "founder, 35 years old, salt-pepper hair, blue knit top"
shot_07: "the man in the home office, navy shirt"
```

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 1. Verbatim character anchors
texto: Even small variations compound. Lock the string. Repeat verbatim.

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 2. Verbatim environment anchors
texto: ## Lock 2. Verbatim environment anchors

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 2. Verbatim environment anchors
texto: Same principle for `series_lock.environment`. The environment string is identical in every shot prompt. The shot's individual subject describes what changes within the environment, not the environment itself.

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 3. Verbatim lighting anchors
texto: ## Lock 3. Verbatim lighting anchors

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 3. Verbatim lighting anchors
texto: Same principle for `series_lock.lighting`. Lighting direction in particular is critical, flipping window-left to window-right between shots produces obvious cuts where there shouldn't be any.

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 5. Reference images (`--cref`, omni-reference, image-to-image)
texto: ## Lock 5. Reference images (`--cref`, omni-reference, image-to-image)

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 5. Reference images (`--cref`, omni-reference, image-to-image)
texto: **Workflow:**

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 5. Reference images (`--cref`, omni-reference, image-to-image)
texto: 1. Generate the hero shot first (any shot, usually `shot_01` or whichever is most defining)

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 5. Reference images (`--cref`, omni-reference, image-to-image)
texto: 2. Use that image as the reference for every subsequent shot

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 5. Reference images (`--cref`, omni-reference, image-to-image)
texto: 3. Each subsequent prompt has the verbatim character anchor PLUS the reference image link

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 5. Reference images (`--cref`, omni-reference, image-to-image)
texto: **This is the most effective lock for character consistency** in 2026. Use it whenever the storyboard features the same person across multiple shots.

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 6. Style references
texto: ## Lock 6. Style references

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 6. Style references
texto: When the storyboard has a distinctive visual style (specific film stock, specific lighting school, specific color theory), use a style reference image:

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 6. Style references
texto: A consistent style reference across all shots produces aesthetic continuity even when characters or environments shift.

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 7. Lighting direction continuity
texto: ## Lock 7. Lighting direction continuity

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 7. Lighting direction continuity
texto: A subtle one that breaks scenes when violated. If `series_lock.lighting` says "soft natural side-light, large window LEFT", then every shot's lighting must respect that direction.

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 7. Lighting direction continuity
texto: When a shot reverses character orientation (e.g., over-the-shoulder reverse), update the rationale to acknowledge the lighting flip:

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 7. Lighting direction continuity
texto:
```
"rationale": "OTS reverse, light source now camera-right (matching scene continuity from window-left in master)"
```

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 7. Lighting direction continuity
texto: If you find yourself flipping light direction without rationale, you're producing visual jump cuts.

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 8. Color grade flow-through
texto: ## Lock 8. Color grade flow-through

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Lock 8. Color grade flow-through
texto: The `series_lock.color_grade` string flows into every prompt verbatim. Same as character/environment/lighting. If shot 1 is "warm filmic, muted teal shadows" and shot 7 is "cinematic teal and orange", the audience will read it as different scenes.

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing
texto: ## Failure modes when locks are missing

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing
texto: | Missing lock | Failure mode |

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing
Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing
texto: | Character | Different person every shot |

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing
texto: | Environment | Scene jumps |

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing
texto: | Lighting | Time-of-day jumps, eye-line breaks |

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing
texto: | Reference image | Loose character interpretation |

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing
texto: | Color grade | Tonal whiplash |

encabezado: Consistency Locks › Failure modes when locks are missing
texto: Every one of these is a production problem editorial cannot fully fix. Lock at the prompt level. Save the editor's time.

encabezado: Consistency Locks › What doesn't work
texto: ## What doesn't work

encabezado: Consistency Locks › What doesn't work
texto: A few things people try that don't actually fix consistency:

encabezado: Consistency Locks › What doesn't work
texto: - **Adding "consistent character" or "same person" to the prompt**, generators don't read meta-instructions

encabezado: Consistency Locks › What doesn't work
texto: - **Numbering shots in the prompt** ("shot 3 of 7, same as before"), generators don't have memory across calls

encabezado: Consistency Locks › What doesn't work
texto: - **Long descriptive paragraphs of the character**, past 4–5 features, the generator starts dropping details randomly

encabezado: Consistency Locks › What doesn't work
texto: - **Asking for "exactly the same"**, there is no such thing in stateless image gen; you reduce drift, you don't eliminate it

encabezado: Consistency Locks › What doesn't work
texto: Accept that some shots will need re-rolls. Budget for it. The locks reduce the failure rate; they don't eliminate it.

encabezado: Failure Modes
texto: # Failure Modes

encabezado: Failure Modes
texto: What goes wrong when generated images don't match the storyboard, and what to fix at the prompt level vs. accept as editorial work.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: ## Failure 1. The "AI look"

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: **Symptoms:** plastic skin, oversaturated colors, eyes too symmetrical, hands wrong, generic stock-photo composition, lighting that's too even, "rendered" feel.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: **Causes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - Generic mood adjectives ("beautiful", "stunning", "amazing")

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - Stable Diffusion crutches ("4k", "highly detailed", "masterpiece") in non-SD generators

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - Missing photographic specifics

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - No "never" list applied from brand-lock

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: **Prompt-level fixes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - Add specific lens and aperture ("50mm prime, f/2.0")

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - Add film stock or camera reference ("Sony FX6", "Kodak Portra 400 film stock")

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - Add "natural skin texture, no AI rendering artifacts" closing line (Flux, GPT Image)

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - Verify brand-lock "never" list is being applied, if it includes "no AI uncanny", surface that into the prompt

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: **Accept editorially when:** the brief is for stylized content where realism isn't the goal.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: ## Failure 2. Character drift across shots

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: **Symptoms:** same person looks different in shot 1 vs shot 5; clothing changes; hair color shifts; age perceived differently.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: **Causes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: - Series_lock character string paraphrased rather than verbatim

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: - No reference image passed (`--cref`, omni-reference)

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: - Too few features described in character anchor (gives generator too much room)

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: **Prompt-level fixes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: - Verify character string is verbatim across every prompt

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: - Add 1–2 more specific features ("small scar above left eyebrow", "black wireframe glasses")

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: - Use reference image after the first successful shot

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: **Accept editorially when:** character consistency is genuinely impossible to lock. Budget re-rolls, typically 2–3× per problematic shot.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: ## Failure 3. Text in image looks bad

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: **Symptoms:** text is misspelled, kerning is off, font is wrong, multiple text elements compete.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: **Causes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: - Text was put in the image prompt instead of being composited

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: - Multiple text elements in one prompt

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: **Prompt-level fixes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: - The right answer is almost always: **don't put text in the prompt**. Composite separately from `text-overlays.json`.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: - Limit to one text element per prompt

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: - Use simple fonts (sans-serif, clean serif), cursive and decorative fonts fail even on Ideogram

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: ## Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: **Symptoms:** shot 3 has light from window-left, shot 4 has light from window-right, they cut together as a continuity error.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: **Causes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: - Lighting language paraphrased rather than verbatim from series_lock

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: - Reverse-angle shots not flagged in rationale

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: - Generator interpreting lighting ambiguously

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: **Prompt-level fixes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: - Verify lighting string is verbatim across prompts

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: - Be explicit about direction: "from camera-left" not "from one side"

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: - For reverse-angle shots, flag in rationale and update lighting language for that shot only

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: - For Flux and GPT Image, add the photographic spec ("key light camera-left at 45 degrees")

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: **Accept editorially when:** lighting drift is subtle enough that color grading will fix it.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: ## Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: **Symptoms:** the storyboard says text goes in the right third, but the generated image has the subject filling the right third.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: **Causes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: - Shot subject didn't include negative-space note

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: - Generator interpreting "centered subject" by default

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: **Prompt-level fixes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: - Add explicit composition note: "subject framed in left third, right two-thirds open for text overlay"

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: - For GPT Image (best at spatial reasoning), use percentage references: "subject at left 30% of frame"

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: - Re-roll with explicit composition prompt, this often fixes on second try

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: **Accept editorially when:** image is otherwise great. Reposition text overlay to fit the actual composition.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: ## Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: **Symptoms:** all locks are in place, prompts look right, but the storyboard feels disjointed when viewed end-to-end.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: **Causes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: - Color grade language drifting between shots (one says "warm filmic", another says "cinematic")

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: - Aspect ratio drift (some 9:16 generations are taller than others)

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: - Mood adjectives shifting ("calm" in shot 1 vs "energetic" in shot 5 even though brief was uniform)

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: **Prompt-level fixes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: - Audit every prompt against series_lock and brand-lock, verbatim check

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: - Verify aspect ratio is identical across all prompts

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: - Lock the brand mood adjectives, same set in every prompt

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: **Accept editorially when:** the disjoint feel is below the noise floor for the medium (e.g. fast-cut social where each shot is on screen <2s).

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: ## Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: **Symptoms:** image is technically good but doesn't capture what the brief was actually about.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: **Causes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: - The shot subject in `shots.json` was vague

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: - The brief context wasn't surfaced into the prompt

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: - The generator is producing competent generic output rather than specific intent

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: **Prompt-level fixes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: - Tighten the shot's subject field, what specifically is the audience meant to feel or notice

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: - Include a one-phrase intent at the end ("the moment of recognition", "the calm before the decision")

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: - For complex scenes, add a "what this shot conveys" line

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: **Accept editorially when:** generation is close enough that retouching gets there. Don't burn API credits chasing perfect on-prompt.

encabezado: Failure Modes › When to stop iterating prompts
texto: ## When to stop iterating prompts

encabezado: Failure Modes › When to stop iterating prompts
texto: Three signs:

encabezado: Failure Modes › When to stop iterating prompts
texto: 1. You've re-rolled the same shot 5+ times with no improvement → the prompt is fine; the model can't render this concept; pick a different shot or different generator

encabezado: Failure Modes › When to stop iterating prompts
texto: 2. You're tweaking single words and hoping → you've hit prompt-level diminishing returns; move to image-to-image refinement (Nano Banana) or post-production

encabezado: Failure Modes › When to stop iterating prompts
texto: 3. The image is 80% right and the gap is editorial → ship to post and let the editor finish

encabezado: Failure Modes › When to stop iterating prompts
texto: Generation is one stage in a pipeline. Don't try to make it the whole pipeline.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers
texto: # Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers
texto: Every image prompt this skill produces is composed from five layers. Four are inputs, one is applied at compose-time. Understanding the layers is the difference between bulletproof prompts and lottery tickets.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: ## Layer 1. Brand Lock

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto:
**What:** the locked brand parameters for the entire project.
**Source:** `brand-lock.snapshot.md` referenced in `shots.json`.
**Constant across:** every storyboard, every shot.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: Contains:

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: - Palette (hex values)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: - Typography (font names, weights)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: - Mood descriptors (3–5 adjectives that describe the brand's emotional posture)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: - "Never" list (things this brand never does, e.g. "no stock photo aesthetic", "no AI uncanny", "no over-saturated", "no shouting copy")

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: - Aspect ratios used

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: - Color grade direction

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: This layer answers: **what does the brand always look and feel like?**

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: ## Layer 2. Series Lock

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto:
**What:** the locked anchors for this specific storyboard.
**Source:** `shots.json` → `series_lock`.
**Constant across:** every shot in this one storyboard.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: Contains:

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: - Character anchor (who's in frame, described identically every shot)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: - Environment description (where the action takes place, identical every shot)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: - Lighting setup (direction, source, color temperature, identical every shot)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: - Color grade (filmic look, identical every shot)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: This layer answers: **what stays the same across this storyboard?**

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: The series_lock is what makes shot 1 and shot 7 feel like the same piece. Without it, every generated frame looks like a different production.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: ## Layer 3. Shot Spec

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto:
**What:** the per-shot variables.
**Source:** `shots.json` → `shots[i]`.
**Variable across:** every shot.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: Contains:

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: - Framing (ECU, CU, MS, etc.)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: - Angle (eye-level, high, low, etc.)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: - Motion (static, push, pull, etc.)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: - Subject (what's happening in this specific shot)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: - Depth of field

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: - Rationale (audit trail, why this shot, this beat, this moment)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: This layer answers: **what's different about this specific shot?**

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto: ## Layer 4. Text Layer

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto:
**What:** on-screen text composited after generation.
**Source:** `text-overlays.json`.
**Never appears in image prompts** (except Ideogram Mode 2 with explicit override).

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto: Why text is a separate layer:

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto: 1. **Editability.** Composited text can be revised without re-generating images.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto: 2. **Quality.** Even Ideogram and GPT Image (the best at text) produce typography that lags professional design tools.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto: 3. **Animation.** Animated text needs After Effects / Remotion / CapCut. Static rendered text is dead-on-arrival for motion content.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto: 4. **Brand control.** Composited text uses exact brand fonts and exact brand colors. Generated text approximates.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto: ## Layer 5. Generator Adapter

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto:
**What:** model-specific syntax wrapper.
**Source:** the relevant `adapters/{generator}.md` file.
**Variable across:** every target generator.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto: This is the only layer the skill *applies* (vs. reads). Layers 1–4 are inputs; Layer 5 is the renderer that turns inputs into a generator-specific string.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto: The adapter handles:

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto: - Length conventions (Seedream short, GPT Image long)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto: - Parameter syntax (`--ar 9:16` vs `aspect_ratio: "9:16"`)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose
texto: ## How layers compose

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose
texto: For a single shot's prompt:

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose
texto:
```
Layer 1 (brand) ───┐
                   │
Layer 2 (series) ──┼──> Layer 5 (adapter) ──> {generator-specific prompt}
                   │
Layer 3 (shot) ────┘

Layer 4 (text) ────> separate compositing pipeline
```

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose
texto: The adapter pulls from Layers 1–3 and produces a string. Layer 4 lives parallel and never enters the prompt.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally
texto: ## Why this matters operationally

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally
texto: **Change the brand color** → edit brand-lock.md. Every prompt across every storyboard updates. No find-and-replace across files.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally
texto: **Change the character** → edit series_lock in shots.json. Every shot in this storyboard updates. Other storyboards untouched.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally
texto: **Change one shot** → edit just that shot's spec. Other shots unaffected.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally
texto: **Change the generator** → swap adapters. Same shot data, different output file. Zero edits to brand-lock or series_lock.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally
texto: **Audit a render** → check brand-lock.snapshot.md to see what version the storyboard was built against.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally
texto: This is why guardrails-in-code beat guardrails-in-vibes. Each layer has one job. Changes are surgical. Outputs are reproducible.
